sentences.zh: 熊概，字元節，豐城人。

translations.literal: Xiong Gai, styled Yuanjie, was a man of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Gai, whose style was Yuanjie, came from Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，隨母適胡氏，冒其姓。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood, he followed his mother in marrying into the Hu family and took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Left fatherless as a boy, he went with his mother when she married into the Hu clan and bore their surname.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongle he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Yongle 9 (1411).

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 十六年擢廣西按察使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted surveillance commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 16 (1418) he was promoted to Guangxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 峒溪蠻大出掠，布政使議請靖江王兵遏之。

translations.literal: The Dongxi tribes came out in force to plunder; the provincial administration commissioner proposed requesting troops from the Prince of Jingjiang to check them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dongxi tribes raided on a large scale, the provincial administration commissioner proposed calling on the Prince of Jingjiang's troops to stop them.

sentences.zh: 概不可，曰：「吾等居方面，寇至無捍禦，顧煩王耶？

translations.literal: Gai would not agree, saying: "We hold regional posts—when bandits arrive and we offer no defense, must we trouble the prince?
translations.idiomatic: Gai objected, saying, "We hold posts in the provinces—if bandits come and we cannot defend, must we trouble the prince?

sentences.zh: 且寇必不至，戒嚴而已。

translations.literal: Moreover the bandits will certainly not come; let us merely stand on alert."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the raiders will surely not come; we need only stand on alert."

sentences.zh: 」已而果然。

translations.literal: " And so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: Events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 久之，調廣東。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年正月，命以原官與布政使周幹、參政葉春巡視南畿、浙江。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Hongxi, he was ordered, retaining his original office, together with administration commissioner Zhou Gan and administration vice commissioner Ye Chun to inspect the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Hongxi 1 (1425), retaining his existing rank, he was ordered with Zhou Gan, administration commissioner, and Ye Chun, administration vice commissioner, to inspect the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 初，夏原吉治水江南還，代以左通政趙居任，兼督農務。

translations.literal: At first, after Xia Yuanji had finished managing the waterways in Jiangnan and returned, Zhao Juren, left assistant commissioner of the Ministry of Works, replaced him and also supervised agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Xia Yuanji had finished his Jiangnan waterworks and returned, he was replaced by Zhao Juren, left assistant commissioner of the Ministry of Works, who also oversaw agricultural affairs.

sentences.zh: 居任不恤民，歲以豐稔聞。

translations.literal: Juren did not care for the people, yet each year reported abundant harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Juren neglected the people yet year after year reported bumper harvests.

sentences.zh: 成祖亦知其誣罔。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor also knew he was deceiving.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengzu knew as well that he was lying.

sentences.zh: 既卒，左通政嶽福繼之，庸懦不事事。

translations.literal: After Juren died, left assistant commissioner Yue Fu succeeded him, timid and inactive in all matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Juren died, Yue Fu succeeded him as left assistant commissioner—timid and unwilling to attend to business.

sentences.zh: 仁宗監國時，嘗命概以御史署刑部，知其賢，故有是命。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent supervised the state, he had once ordered Gai, as a censor, to act at the Ministry of Punishments and knew him to be capable; hence this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: While the heir apparent was supervising the realm, he had once had Gai serve at the Ministry of Punishments in his capacity as censor and knew him to be able; hence this order.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，幹還，言有司多不得人，土豪肆惡，而福不任職。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year Gan returned and reported that many local officials were unfit, local bullies ran rampant, and Fu was not performing his duties.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the eighth month Gan returned and reported that many local officials were incompetent, powerful local bullies ran wild, and Fu was not doing his job.

sentences.zh: 宣宗召福還，擢概大理寺卿，與春同往巡撫。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor recalled Fu and promoted Gai to chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review, and he went with Ye Chun to serve as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuande recalled Fu and promoted Gai to chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review; he and Ye Chun then went out as grand coordinators.

sentences.zh: 南畿、浙江設巡撫自此始。

translations.literal: The establishment of grand coordinators for the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators for the Southern Metropolitan Region and Zhejiang date from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 浙西豪持郡邑短長為不法。

translations.literal: Powerful families in western Zhejiang held the faults of prefectures and counties over them and acted lawlessly.
translations.idiomatic: In western Zhejiang, great clans used knowledge of local officials' failings to break the law with impunity.

sentences.zh: 海鹽民平康暴橫甚，御史捕之，遁去。

translations.literal: The salt-worker Ping Kang was extremely violent and overbearing; when a censor arrested him, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: The salt laborer Ping Kang was wildly brutal; a censor seized him, but he escaped.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，益聚黨八百余人。

translations.literal: When an amnesty brought him back, he gathered more than eight hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty restored him, he mustered a band of more than eight hundred men.

sentences.zh: 概捕誅之。

translations.literal: Gai captured and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 已，悉捕豪惡數十輩，械至京，論如法。

translations.literal: Thereafter he arrested dozens of powerful evildoers, sent them in cangues to the capital, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrested dozens of powerful wrongdoers, shackled them to the capital, and punished them as the law required.

sentences.zh: 於是奸宄帖息。

translations.literal: Thereupon treachery and villainy were subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Wickedness and crime were brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 諸衛所糧運不繼，軍乏食。

translations.literal: Grain transport at the various guard units could not keep up, and the troops lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Grain shipments to the guard units fell behind, and the soldiers went hungry.

sentences.zh: 概以便宜發諸府贖罪米四萬二千余石贍軍，乃聞於朝。

translations.literal: Gai on his own authority released more than forty-two thousand piculs of fine-grain rice from redemption-of-punishment levies in the various prefectures to feed the army, and only then reported to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Gai on emergency authority drew more than forty-two thousand piculs of commutation grain from the prefectures to provision the troops, then reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，諭戶部勿以專擅罪概。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and instructed the Ministry of Revenue not to punish Gai for acting on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and told the Ministry of Revenue not to charge Gai with overstepping his authority.

sentences.zh: 概用法嚴，奸民憚之，騰謗書於朝。

translations.literal: Gai enforced the law strictly; lawless commoners feared him and circulated slanderous writings at court.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gai applied the law harshly, criminals feared him and sent libelous memorials to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，行在都御史劾概與春所至作威福，縱兵擾民。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xuande, the acting censor-in-chief at the capital impeached Gai and Ye Chun for throwing their weight about wherever they went and letting soldiers harass the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 2 (1427), the acting censor-in-chief at the capital impeached Gai and Ye Chun for lording it over the regions they visited and allowing troops to harass the people.

sentences.zh: 帝弗問，陰使御史廉之，無所得。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not pursue the matter but secretly sent censors to investigate; nothing was found.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not inquire further but quietly sent censors to look into it; they found nothing.

sentences.zh: 由是益任概。

translations.literal: From this he trusted Gai all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he relied on Gai all the more.

sentences.zh: 明年七月賜璽書獎勵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he was granted an imperial letter of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the next year he received an imperial commendation bearing the seal.

sentences.zh: 概亦自信，諸當興革者皆列以聞。

translations.literal: Gai also grew confident and reported everything that should be instituted or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gai grew confident as well and memorialized on every matter that should be reformed or abolished.

sentences.zh: 時屢遣部官至江南造紙、市銅鐵。

translations.literal: At the time ministry officials were repeatedly sent to Jiangnan to manufacture paper and purchase copper and iron.
translations.idiomatic: At the time officials from the ministries were repeatedly sent to Jiangnan to make paper and buy copper and iron.

sentences.zh: 概言水澇民饑，乞罷之。

translations.literal: Gai said floods had afflicted the people and begged that these missions be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gai reported that floods had left the people in distress and asked that the work be halted.

sentences.zh: 五年還朝，始復姓。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he returned to court and at last resumed his original surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to the capital and finally took back his own surname.

sentences.zh: 亡何，遷右都御史，治南院事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to right censor-in-chief and managed affairs of the southern court.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made right censor-in-chief and directed the southern branch of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 行在都御史顧佐疾，驛召概代領其職，兼署刑部。

translations.literal: When acting censor-in-chief Gu Zuo fell ill, Gai was summoned by courier to take over his duties and also act at the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the acting censor-in-chief Gu Zuo fell ill, Gai was summoned by express relay to head the office and also serve at the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 九年十月錄囚，自朝至日宴，未暇食，忽風眩卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the ninth year, while reviewing prisoners, from morning until the banquet at day's end he had no time to eat; suddenly he was struck by wind dizziness and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the ninth year, as he was reviewing prisoners from morning until the evening feast without time to eat, he was suddenly seized by vertigo and died.

sentences.zh: 賜祭，給舟歸其喪。

translations.literal: The court granted sacrificial offerings and provided a boat to return his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted funeral sacrifices and sent a boat to carry his coffin home.

sentences.zh: 概性剛決，巡視江南，威名甚盛。

translations.literal: Gai was by nature firm and decisive; in touring Jiangnan his prestige was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was firm and resolute by nature; on his tours of Jiangnan his authority was immense.

sentences.zh: 及掌臺憲，聲稱漸損於初。

translations.literal: When he took charge of the censorate, his reputation gradually fell short of what it had been at first.
translations.idiomatic: Once he headed the censorate, his renown gradually fell short of what it had been at first.

sentences.zh: 葉春者，海鹽人。

translations.literal: As for Ye Chun, he was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chun was a native of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 起家掾吏，歷禮部郎中兩淮鹽運使，改四川右參政。

translations.literal: He rose from clerk, served as a director in the Ministry of Rites and as salt transport commissioner for the two Huai circuits, and was transferred to right administration vice commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk, rose to director in the Ministry of Rites and commissioner of salt transport for the two Huai circuits, and was transferred to right administration vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 與概巡撫江、浙諸府。

translations.literal: Together with Gai he grand-coordinated the prefectures of Jiangsu and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Gai he grand-coordinated the Jiangsu and Zhejiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 既復奉命與錦衣指揮任啟、御史賴英、太監劉寧巡視。

translations.literal: He was again ordered, together with Jin Yi guard commander Ren Qi, investigating censor Lai Ying, and eunuch Liu Ning, to conduct an inspection tour.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered, with Jin Yi guard commander Ren Qi, investigating censor Lai Ying, and eunuch Liu Ning, to conduct an inspection tour.

sentences.zh: 先後凡三蒞浙西，治事於鄉，人無議其私者。

translations.literal: In all he came to western Zhejiang three times and conducted affairs in his home district; no one criticized him for partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Three times in succession he came to western Zhejiang and handled affairs in his home region, yet no one accused him of favoritism.

sentences.zh: 概遷都御史。

translations.literal: When Gai was transferred to censor-in-chief,
translations.idiomatic: When Gai was made censor-in-chief,

sentences.zh: 春同日進刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Chun was promoted the same day to right vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was promoted the same day to right vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 陳鎰，字有戒，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Chen Yi, styled Youjie, was a man of Wu county.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi, whose style was Youjie, came from Wu county.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年進士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongle he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Yongle 10 (1412).

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 遷湖廣副使，歷山東、浙江，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Huguang and served in Shandong and Zhejiang, winning renown in each.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner of Huguang and served in Shandong and Zhejiang, earning a reputation in each post.

sentences.zh: 九年春進右都御史，鎮守如故。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he was advanced to right censor-in-chief while continuing to command the garrison as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he was promoted to right censor-in-chief while continuing to command the garrison as before.

sentences.zh: 秦中饑，乞蠲租十之四，其余米布兼收。

translations.literal: Qin was suffering famine; he requested remission of one-fourth of the land tax, with the remainder collected in grain and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: With famine in Shaanxi, he asked that one-fourth of the land tax be remitted and the rest collected in grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 時瓦剌也先漸強，遣人授罕東諸衛都督喃哥等為平章，又置甘肅行省名號。

translations.literal: At the time Oirat leader Esen was growing stronger; he sent men to invest Nangor and other commanders of the Han East guard with the title of pingzhang, and also set up the name of a Gansu provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Oirat leader Esen was growing stronger; he sent men to invest Nangor and other commanders of the Han East guard with the title of pingzhang and even established the name of a Gansu provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 鎰以聞，請嚴為之備。

translations.literal: Yi reported this and asked that strict precautions be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reported it and urged strict precautions.

sentences.zh: 已，命與靖遠伯王驥巡視甘肅、寧夏、延綏邊務，聽便宜處置。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji, to inspect border affairs in Gansu, Ningxia, and Yan-sui, with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered, with Jingyuan Earl Wang Ji, to inspect border affairs in Gansu, Ningxia, and Yan-sui with discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 以災沴頻仍，條上撫安軍民二十四事，多議行。

translations.literal: Because disasters were frequent, he submitted twenty-four measures to pacify troops and civilians, most of which were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: With disasters recurring, he submitted twenty-four measures to pacify soldiers and civilians; most were adopted.

sentences.zh: 鎰嘗恐襄、漢間流民嘯聚為亂，請命河南、湖廣、陜西三司官親至其地撫恤之。

translations.literal: Yi had once feared that displaced people between Xiang and Han might gather and rise in revolt, and asked that officials of the Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi administrations go in person to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had once feared that refugees between the Xiang and Han rivers might band together in revolt and asked that officials of the Henan, Huguang, and Shaanxi administrations go in person to comfort them.

sentences.zh: 得旨允行，而當事者不以為意。

translations.literal: The order was approved, but those in charge paid it no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved, but those responsible paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 王文亦相繼力言有司怠忽，恐遺禍。

translations.literal: Wang Wen also repeatedly pressed the point that local officials were negligent and feared disaster would follow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wen likewise pressed repeatedly that local officials were slack and that calamity might follow.

sentences.zh: 至成化時，乃有項忠之役，人益思鎰言。

translations.literal: Only in the Chenghua reign did Xiang Zhong's campaign occur, and people came to value Yi's words all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the Chenghua reign did Xiang Zhong's campaign take place, and people valued Yi's warning all the more.

sentences.zh: 英宗北狩，景帝監國，鎰合大臣廷論王振。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was taken north on campaign, Emperor Jingdi supervised the realm; Yi joined the great ministers in court debate on Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong was carried off on the northern campaign, Emperor Jingdi supervised the realm; Yi joined the senior ministers in court debate on Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 於是振侄王山伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Zhen's nephew Wang Shan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen's nephew Wang Shan was then executed.

sentences.zh: 也先將入犯，以于謙薦，出撫畿內。

translations.literal: When Esen was about to invade, on Yu Qian's recommendation Yi was sent out to pacify the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: As Esen was about to invade, on Yu Qian's recommendation Yi was sent out to pacify the capital region.

sentences.zh: 事寧，召還，進左都御史。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was recalled and promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When peace returned he was recalled and made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年，陜西饑，軍民萬余人，「願得陳公活我。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jingtai reign Shaanxi suffered famine; more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians cried, "We wish Lord Chen to keep us alive."
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 2 (1451), with famine in Shaanxi, more than ten thousand soldiers and civilians pleaded, "We wish Lord Chen would keep us alive."

sentences.zh: 」監司以聞，帝復命之。

translations.literal: " The supervising officials reported this, and the Emperor again sent him.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising officials reported it, and the Emperor again sent him out.

sentences.zh: 鎰至是凡三鎮陜，先後十余年，陜人戴之若父母。

translations.literal: By then Yi had governed Shaanxi three times in all, more than ten years in total; the people of Shaanxi revered him as they would their parents.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yi had governed Shaanxi three times in all, for more than ten years altogether; the people of Shaanxi revered him as parents.

sentences.zh: 每還朝，必遮道擁車泣。

translations.literal: Whenever he returned to court they would block the road, surround his carriage, and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he returned to the capital they blocked the road, pressed around his carriage, and wept.

sentences.zh: 再至，則歡迎數百里不絕。

translations.literal: When he came again, they welcomed him for hundreds of li without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When he came again, they welcomed him for hundreds of li without end.

sentences.zh: 其得軍民心，前後撫陜者莫及也。

translations.literal: In winning the hearts of soldiers and civilians, no previous or later governor of Shaanxi matched him.
translations.idiomatic: In winning the hearts of troops and people, no governor of Shaanxi before or after equaled him.

sentences.zh: 三年春召還，加太子太保，與王文並掌都察院。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was recalled and made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, sharing direction of the censorate with Wang Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was recalled, made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and shared direction of the censorate with Wang Wen.

sentences.zh: 文威嚴，諸御史畏之若神。

translations.literal: Wen was stern and awesome; the censors feared him as they would a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was stern and imposing; the censors feared him like a god.

sentences.zh: 鎰性寬恕，少風裁，譽望損於在陜時。

translations.literal: Yi was forgiving by nature and showed little disciplinary rigor; his reputation fell short of what it had been in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was forgiving by nature and exercised little discipline; his standing fell short of what it had been in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 明年秋以疾致仕。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the following year he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the next year he retired because of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，謚僖敏。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Ximin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Ximin.

sentences.zh: 天順七年，詔官其子伸為刑部照磨。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of the Tianshun reign an edict appointed his son Shen registrar of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 7 (1463) an edict appointed his son Shen registrar of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 李儀，涿人。

translations.literal: Li Yi, a man of Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi came from Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 永樂間以薦舉授戶部主事。

translations.literal: During Yongle he was appointed principal clerk of the Ministry of Revenue on recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle reign he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue by recommendation.

sentences.zh: 宣宗既平高煦，義請去趙王護衛。

translations.literal: After the Xuande Emperor had pacified Gao Xu, Yi requested removal of the Prince of Zhao's guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Xuande had put down Gao Xu, Yi asked that the Prince of Zhao's guard be removed.

sentences.zh: 尚書張本亦言：「往歲孟賢謀逆，趙王未必不知。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Ben also said: "In past years Meng Xian plotted rebellion; the Prince of Zhao may not have been ignorant of it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Ben also said, "When Meng Xian plotted rebellion in earlier years, the Prince of Zhao may well have known.

sentences.zh: 高煦亦謂與趙合謀。

translations.literal: Gao Xu also said he had conspired with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xu likewise claimed he had plotted with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 儀言是。

translations.literal: Yi said this was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Yi agreed.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 既而言者益眾。

translations.literal: Before long those who spoke on the matter grew more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Before long more and more officials spoke up.

sentences.zh: 帝封其詞，遣使諭王如儀指。

translations.literal: The Emperor sealed their memorials and sent envoys to instruct the prince as Yi had indicated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sealed up their memorials and sent envoys to instruct the prince along the lines Yi had proposed.

sentences.zh: 王即獻護衛，趙卒無事。

translations.literal: The prince at once surrendered his guard, and Zhao was spared trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The prince immediately surrendered his guard, and Zhao was spared further trouble.

sentences.zh: 儀尋出知九江府，有惠政。

translations.literal: Before long Yi went out as prefect of Jiujiang, where he carried out benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was soon sent out as prefect of Jiujiang, where his rule was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位之歲，始設諸邊巡撫。

translations.literal: In the year Emperor Yingzong took the throne, grand coordinators were first established on the various frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Yingzong came to the throne, frontier grand coordinators were established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史丁璿方督大同、宣府軍儲，而儀以右僉都御史巡撫其地，盛有所建置。

translations.literal: Vice censor-in-chief Ding Xuan was then supervising military grain stores at Datong and Xuanfu, while Yi, as right vice censor-in-chief, grand-coordinated the region and achieved much.
translations.idiomatic: While Ding Xuan, vice censor-in-chief, was supervising military grain at Datong and Xuanfu, Yi served as right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator there and accomplished a great deal.

sentences.zh: 明年請以大同東西二路分責於總兵官羅文、方政。

translations.literal: The following year he asked that the eastern and western routes of Datong be assigned separately to the supreme commanders Luo Wen and Fang Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he asked that Datong's eastern and western routes be divided between supreme commanders Luo Wen and Fang Zheng.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 時朝議遣方政、楊洪出塞，與甘肅將蔣貴、史昭合擊朵兒只伯。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated sending Fang Zheng and Yang Hong beyond the passes, together with Gansu generals Jiang Gui and Shi Zhao, to strike Dorjiban jointly.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated sending Fang Zheng and Yang Hong beyond the passes to join Gansu generals Jiang Gui and Shi Zhao in a joint strike on Dorjiban.

sentences.zh: 儀言：「四裔為患，自古有之，在備禦有方耳。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The four barbarians have been a trouble since antiquity; what matters is having sound defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Barbarians on the four sides have troubled China since antiquity; what matters is sound defense.

sentences.zh: 和寧殘部，窮無所歸，乍臣乍叛，小為邊寇。

translations.literal: The remnant of Hening, with nowhere left to flee, now submits and now rebels, making small raids on the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Hening remnant, with nowhere left to flee, now submits and now rebels, raiding the border in small bands.

sentences.zh: 邊將謹待之，將自遁，何必窮兵。

translations.literal: If frontier generals treat them carefully, they will flee of themselves—why exhaust the army?
translations.idiomatic: If frontier generals treat them carefully, they will withdraw on their own—why exhaust the army?

sentences.zh: 萬一乘虛襲我，少有失，適足為笑，乞敕政等無窮追。

translations.literal: If by chance they strike us when we are exposed, the slightest loss will be enough to make us a laughingstock; I beg that Zheng and the others be ordered not to pursue to the end."
translations.idiomatic: If they should strike when we are exposed, the least setback would make us a laughingstock; I beg that Zheng and the others be ordered not to pursue to the end."

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: " This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The advice was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 督糧參政劉璉不職，儀劾之。

translations.literal: Grain-supervising administration vice commissioner Liu Lian was derelict; Yi impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lian, the grain-supervising administration vice commissioner, was incompetent, and Yi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 璉乃誣儀淫亂事。

translations.literal: Lian then falsely accused Yi of sexual misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Lian then falsely accused Yi of sexual misconduct.

sentences.zh: 適參將石亨欲奏鎮守中官郭敬罪，先咨儀。

translations.literal: Just then participating general Shi Heng wished to memorialize on the crimes of the garrison eunuch Guo Jing and first consulted Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time participating general Shi Heng wished to memorialize against garrison eunuch Guo Jing and first consulted Yi.

sentences.zh: 儀誤緘咨牒於核餉主事文卷中，戶部以聞，致亨、敬相奏訐。

translations.literal: Yi mistakenly sealed the consultation document among the papers of the chief clerk who audited provisions; the Ministry of Revenue reported it, leading Heng and Jing to accuse each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yi mistakenly sealed the consultation among the papers of the chief clerk who audited provisions; the Ministry of Revenue reported it, and Heng and Jing accused each other.

sentences.zh: 詔儀、璉自陳，而切責敬等。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi and Lian to explain themselves while sharply rebuking Jing and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yi and Lian to explain themselves while sharply rebuking Jing and the others.

sentences.zh: 璉止停俸二歲。

translations.literal: Lian was only fined two years' salary.
translations.idiomatic: Lian was only fined two years' salary.

sentences.zh: 儀雖引罪，自負其直，詞頗激，遂被劾下吏瘐死。

translations.literal: Although Yi pleaded guilty, confident in his integrity his words were rather heated, and he was impeached, sent down to the law officers, and died in prison of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yi admitted fault, confident in his integrity his words were sharp; he was impeached, sent to the law officers, and died in prison of illness.

sentences.zh: 正統二年二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the second month of the second year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second month of Zhengtong 2 (1437).

sentences.zh: 儀居官廉謹，邊人素德之。

translations.literal: Yi in office was honest and careful, and the frontier people had long respected him.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yi was honest and careful, and the frontier people had long respected him.

sentences.zh: 聞其死，建昭德祠以祀。

translations.literal: When they heard of his death they built the Zhaode Shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard of his death they built the Zhaode Shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 丁璿，上元人。

translations.literal: Ding Xuan, a man of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xuan came from Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 永樂中進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi during Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 由御史擢居是職。

translations.literal: From investigating censor he was promoted to this post.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from investigating censor to this post.

sentences.zh: 正統五年將征麓川，命乘傳往備儲餉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong, when an expedition against Luchuan was planned, he was ordered to travel by express relay to prepare stores and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 5 (1440), as an expedition against Luchuan was planned, he was ordered to travel by express relay to prepare stores and provisions.

sentences.zh: 尋言用兵便宜，遂命撫雲南。

translations.literal: Soon he spoke on the conveniences of using troops and was ordered to pacify Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he spoke on military expedients and was ordered to pacify Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 麓川平，召為左副都御史，所至有聲。

translations.literal: When Luchuan was pacified he was recalled as left vice censor-in-chief and wherever he went won renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Luchuan was pacified he was recalled as left vice censor-in-chief; wherever he went he won renown.

sentences.zh: 陳泰，字吉亨，光澤人。

translations.literal: Chen Tai, styled Jiheng, was a man of Guangze.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tai, whose style was Jiheng, came from Guangze.

sentences.zh: 幼從外家曹姓，既貴，乃復故。

translations.literal: In childhood he followed his mother's family, the Caos, in their surname; once he rose high he resumed his original name.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he took his mother's Cao surname; once he rose high he resumed his own.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一，除安慶府學訓導。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination and was appointed instructor at Anqing prefectural school.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the provincial examinations and was made instructor at the Anqing prefectural school.

sentences.zh: 正統初，廷臣交薦，擢御史，巡按貴州。

translations.literal: At the start of Zhengtong, court officials jointly recommended him; he was raised to investigating censor and sent to inspect Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhengtong, court officials jointly recommended him; he was made investigating censor and sent to inspect Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 官軍征麓川，歲取土兵二千為鄉導，戰失利，輒殺以冒功，泰奏罷之。

translations.literal: When government troops campaigned against Luchuan they took two thousand native soldiers each year as guides; when battles went badly they would kill them to claim merit—Tai memorialized to stop this.
translations.idiomatic: When government troops campaigned against Luchuan they took two thousand native soldiers yearly as guides; when battles went badly they killed them to claim merit—Tai memorialized to stop this.

sentences.zh: 再按山西。

translations.literal: He inspected Shanxi a second time.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Shanxi again.

sentences.zh: 時百官俸薄，折鈔又不能即得。

translations.literal: At the time official salaries were thin, and paper-money conversion could not be obtained at once.
translations.idiomatic: At the time official salaries were meager, and paper-money conversion could not be obtained promptly.

sentences.zh: 泰上章乞量增祿廩，俾足養廉，然後治贓汙，則貪風自息。

translations.literal: Tai memorialized asking that salaries and grain rations be increased enough to sustain integrity, and only then to punish corruption, so that greedy ways would cease of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Tai memorialized asking that salaries and grain be increased enough to sustain integrity; only then, he said, should corruption be punished, and greedy ways would cease of themselves.

sentences.zh: 事格不行。

translations.literal: The matter was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was blocked and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 六年夏言：「連歲災異，咎在廷臣，請敕御史給事中糾彈大臣，去其尤不職者，而後所司各考核其屬。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he said: "Disasters and portents have come year after year; the fault lies with court ministers. I ask that investigating censors and supervising secretaries be ordered to impeach the great ministers, remove the most derelict, and only then let each office examine its subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year he said, "Disasters have come year after year; the fault lies with court ministers. I ask that censors and supervising secretaries be ordered to impeach the senior ministers, remove the most derelict, and only then let each office examine its subordinates."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是御史馬謹等交章劾吏部尚書郭琎等數十人。

translations.literal: Thereupon investigating censor Ma Jin and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Minister of Personnel Guo Jin and several dozen others.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon investigating censor Ma Jin and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Minister of Personnel Guo Jin and several dozen others.

sentences.zh: 已，復出按山東。

translations.literal: Before long he went out again to inspect Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went out again to inspect Shandong.

sentences.zh: 泰素勵操行，好搏擊。

translations.literal: Tai had always cultivated his conduct and liked to strike blows.
translations.idiomatic: Tai had always cultivated his conduct and liked to take bold action.

sentences.zh: 三為巡按，懲奸去貪，威棱甚峻。

translations.literal: Three times as inspecting censor he punished the wicked and removed the greedy; his authority was very stern.
translations.idiomatic: Three times as inspecting censor he punished the wicked and removed the greedy; his authority was very stern.

sentences.zh: 九年超擢四川按察使，與鎮守都御史寇深相失。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted over the regular steps to surveillance commissioner of Sichuan and fell out with garrison censor-in-chief Kou Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was promoted over the regular steps to Sichuan surveillance commissioner and fell out with garrison censor-in-chief Kou Shen.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月，參議陳敏希深指，劾泰擅杖武職，毆輿夫至死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, administration vice commissioner Chen Min, currying favor with Shen, impeached Tai for arbitrarily beating military officers and beating a sedan bearer to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, administration vice commissioner Chen Min, currying favor with Shen, impeached Tai for arbitrarily beating military officers and beating a sedan bearer to death.

sentences.zh: 逮刑部獄，坐斬。

translations.literal: He was seized and sent to the Ministry of Punishments prison and sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He was seized and sent to the Ministry of Punishments and sentenced to decapitation.

sentences.zh: 泰奏辯，大理卿俞士悅亦具狀以聞。

translations.literal: Tai memorialized in his defense; Court of Judicial Review chief minister Yu Shiyue also submitted a full report.
translations.idiomatic: Tai memorialized in his defense; Court of Judicial Review chief minister Yu Shiyue also submitted a full report.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: Neither was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Neither was heeded.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，赦復官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi supervised the realm, an amnesty restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi supervised the realm, an amnesty restored his office.

sentences.zh: 于謙薦守紫荊關。

translations.literal: On Yu Qian's recommendation he was ordered to defend Zijing Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On Yu Qian's recommendation he was ordered to defend Zijing Pass.

sentences.zh: 也先入犯，關門不守，復論死。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded, the pass was not held and he was again sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded, the pass was not held and he was again sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 景帝宥之，命充為事官，從總兵官顧興祖築關隘自效。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingdi pardoned him and ordered him to serve as an officer on probation, following supreme commander Gu Xingzu in building passes and forts to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingdi pardoned him and ordered him to serve on probation, following supreme commander Gu Xingzu in building passes and forts to redeem himself.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年擢大理右少卿，守備白羊口。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he was promoted right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and ordered to defend Baiyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 1 (1450) he was promoted right vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review and ordered to defend Baiyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 四月，都督同知劉安代寧遠伯任禮巡備涿、易、真、保諸城，命泰以右僉都御史參其軍務。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, when Vice Commissioner-in-chief Liu An replaced Ningyuan Earl Ren Li in patrolling Zhuo, Yi, Zhen, and Bao and the other cities, Tai was ordered as right vice censor-in-chief to join in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, when Vice Commissioner-in-chief Liu An replaced Ningyuan Earl Ren Li in patrolling Zhuo, Yi, Zhen, Bao, and the other cities, Tai was ordered as right vice censor-in-chief to join the military staff.

sentences.zh: 三年兼巡撫保定六府。

translations.literal: In the third year he was also made grand coordinator of the six prefectures of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was also made grand coordinator of Baoding's six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 尋命督治河道。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise river works.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to supervise river works.

sentences.zh: 自儀真至淮安，浚渠百八十里，塞決口九，築壩三，役六萬人，數月而畢。

translations.literal: From Yizhen to Huai'an he dredged channels for one hundred and eighty li, blocked nine breaches, built three dams, and employed sixty thousand men, finishing in several months.
translations.idiomatic: From Yizhen to Huai'an he dredged channels for one hundred and eighty li, blocked nine breaches, built three dams, and employed sixty thousand men, finishing in several months.

sentences.zh: 七年移撫蘇、松。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 天順改元，罷巡撫官，改廣東副使，以憂去。

translations.literal: When the Tianshun reign began, grand coordinator posts were abolished; he was made vice commissioner of Guangdong and left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianshun reign began, grand coordinator posts were abolished; he was made Guangdong vice commissioner and left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 四川盜起，有言泰嘗蒞其地，有威名，乃復故官，往巡撫。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Sichuan, some said Tai had once served there and had a formidable reputation; he was restored to his former office and sent to grand-coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Sichuan, some said Tai had once served there and had a formidable reputation; he was restored to his former rank and sent to grand-coordinate.

sentences.zh: 八年進右副都御史，總督漕運兼巡撫淮、揚諸府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief, director-general of grain transport, and grand coordinator of Huai and Yang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was advanced to right vice censor-in-chief, director-general of grain transport, and grand coordinator of Huai and Yang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蒞淮三年，謝政歸。

translations.literal: After three years at Huai he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After three years at Huai he retired and returned home.

sentences.zh: 成化六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chenghua 6 (1470).

sentences.zh: 李棠，字宗楷，縉雲人。

translations.literal: Li Tang, styled Zongkai, was a man of Jinyun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang, whose style was Zongkai, came from Jinyun.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Xuande 5 (1430).

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，為尚書魏源所器。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk of the Ministry of Punishments and was valued by Minister Wei Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and was valued by Minister Wei Yuan.

sentences.zh: 金濂代源，以剛嚴懾下。

translations.literal: When Jin Lian replaced Yuan, he intimidated his subordinates with harsh severity.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Lian replaced Yuan, he intimidated his subordinates with harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 棠與辯論是非，譴訶不為動，濂亦器之。

translations.literal: Tang debated right and wrong with him; though rebuked and scolded he did not waver, and Lian also came to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang debated right and wrong with him; though rebuked and scolded he did not waver, and Lian came to respect him as well.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 錄囚南畿，多所平反，進郎中。

translations.literal: While reviewing prisoners in the Southern Metropolitan Region he reversed many wrongful convictions and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: While reviewing prisoners in the Southern Metropolitan Region he reversed many wrongful convictions and was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 景帝嗣位，超擢本部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi succeeded, he was promoted over the regular steps to vice minister of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingdi succeeded, he was promoted over the regular steps to vice minister of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡撫廣西，提督軍務。

translations.literal: Before long he grand-coordinated Guangxi and directed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he grand-coordinated Guangxi and directed military affairs.

sentences.zh: 所部多寇，棠以次討平之。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction had many bandits; Tang suppressed them one after another.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction had many bandits; Tang suppressed them in succession.

sentences.zh: 正己帥下，令行政舉。

translations.literal: He rectified himself and led his subordinates, ordering that administration be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He rectified himself and led his subordinates, ordering that administration be carried out.

sentences.zh: 景泰三年，思明土知府黃老，子鈞嗣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingtai, Huang Lao, native prefect of Siming, was succeeded by his son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 3 (1452), Huang Lao, native prefect of Siming, was succeeded by his son Jun.

sentences.zh: 庶兄矰使其子殺父子，滅其家，而以他盜為亂告。

translations.literal: A cousin Zeng had his son kill father and son, exterminated the family, and reported other bandits as the culprits.
translations.idiomatic: A cousin Zeng had his son kill father and son, exterminate the family, and report other bandits as the culprits.

sentences.zh: 棠檄右參政曾翚副使劉仁宅按其事。

translations.literal: Tang sent a dispatch ordering right administration vice commissioner Zeng Hui and surveillance vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang sent a dispatch ordering right administration vice commissioner Zeng Hui and surveillance vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate.

sentences.zh: 翚等誘執矰父子下之獄。

translations.literal: Hui and the others lured Zeng and his son into custody and sent them to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and the others lured Zeng and his son into custody and sent them to prison.

sentences.zh: 矰窘則遣使走京師，上書請帝廢太子立己子。

translations.literal: Hard pressed, Zeng sent an envoy to the capital and memorialized asking the Emperor to depose the heir apparent and establish his own son.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Zeng sent an envoy to the capital memorializing that the Emperor depose the heir apparent and establish his own son.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，立擢矰都督同知，出其子於獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased, immediately promoted Zeng to vice commissioner-in-chief, and released his son from prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased, immediately promoted Zeng to vice commissioner-in-chief, and released his son from prison.

sentences.zh: 事具《懷獻太子》及《土司傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is given in full in the biographies of the Deposed Heir Apparent and the Native Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is given in full in the biographies of the Deposed Heir Apparent and the Native Offices.

sentences.zh: 棠既不得竟黃矰獄，郁郁累疏謝病歸。

translations.literal: Tang, unable to bring the Huang Zeng case to completion, repeatedly memorialized to resign on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bring the Huang Zeng case to completion, Tang repeatedly memorialized to resign on grounds of illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 不攜嶺表一物，以清節顯。

translations.literal: He took not a single thing from the Lingnan region and was known for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He took not a single thing from the Lingnan region and was known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 曾翚，字時升，泰和人。

translations.literal: Zeng Hui, styled Shisheng, was a man of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Hui, whose style was Shisheng, came from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Xuande 8 (1433).

sentences.zh: 治秦府永興王葬，卻有司饋遺。

translations.literal: He oversaw the burial of the Prince of Qin's Yongxing prince and refused gifts from the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the burial of the Qin prince's Yongxing heir and refused gifts from the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尚書金濂器之，俾典奏牘。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Lian valued him and had him manage memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Lian valued him and had him manage memorials.

sentences.zh: 有重獄，諸郎不能決，輒以屬翚。

translations.literal: When there was a weighty case that the various directors could not decide, it was always assigned to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: When there was a weighty case the various directors could not decide, it was always assigned to Hui.

sentences.zh: 秦王訐巡撫陳鎰狎妓。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin accused grand coordinator Chen Yi of consorting with prostitutes.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin accused grand coordinator Chen Yi of consorting with prostitutes.

sentences.zh: 翚按得其情，劾藩府誣大臣，鎰得白。

translations.literal: Hui investigated and obtained the facts, impeaching the princely establishment for slandering a great minister; Yi was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Hui investigated and obtained the facts, impeaching the princely establishment for slandering a great minister, and Yi was cleared.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進郎中。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhengtong he was advanced to director.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 13 (1448) he was promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 以何文淵薦，擢廣西右參政。

translations.literal: On He Wenyuan's recommendation he was raised to right administration vice commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: On He Wenyuan's recommendation he was made right administration vice commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 李棠檄翚及副使劉仁宅按黃矰父子。

translations.literal: Li Tang dispatched Hui and surveillance vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate Huang Zeng and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tang dispatched Hui and surveillance vice commissioner Liu Renzhai to investigate Huang Zeng and his son.

sentences.zh: 矰使人持千金賄於道，且擁精兵挾之。

translations.literal: Zeng sent men to offer a thousand taels of gold in bribes on the road and also brought elite troops to intimidate them.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng sent men to offer a thousand taels of gold as bribes along the road and brought elite troops to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 二人佯許諾，已，誘執矰下之獄。

translations.literal: The two men pretended to agree; then they lured Zeng into custody and sent him to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The two pretended to agree; then they lured Zeng into custody and sent him to prison.

sentences.zh: 棠以聞。

translations.literal: Tang reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Tang reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 未幾，矰以上書擢都督同知，父子俱出獄，翚等太息而已。

translations.literal: Before long Zeng, by memorializing, was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief; father and son both left prison, and Hui and the others could only sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zeng, by memorializing, was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief; father and son were both released, and Hui and the others could only sigh.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去。

translations.literal: Soon he left on mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he left on mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起官河南御史。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled as investigating censor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled as Henan investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 清軍者利得軍，多枉及民，翚辨釋甚眾。

translations.literal: Those who cleared troops profited by obtaining soldiers and often wrongfully implicated civilians; Hui exonerated very many.
translations.idiomatic: Those who cleared troops profited by seizing soldiers and often wrongfully implicated civilians; Hui exonerated a great many.

sentences.zh: 南陽諸府多流戶，眾議驅逐，人情惶急，翚與巡撫撫安之。

translations.literal: The prefectures around Nanyang had many displaced households; many proposed expelling them, and the people were in panic; Hui, together with the grand coordinator, pacified and settled them.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanyang prefectures had many displaced households; many proposed expelling them and the people were in panic; Hui, with the grand coordinator, pacified and settled them.

sentences.zh: 天順五年遷山東右布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianshun he was transferred to right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 5 (1461) he was transferred to right administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 民墾田無賦者，奸民指為閑田，獻諸戚畹。

translations.literal: Land the people had reclaimed but for which no tax was levied was pointed out by scoundrels as idle land and presented to imperial in-laws.
translations.idiomatic: Land the people had reclaimed without tax was pointed out by scoundrels as idle land and presented to imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 部使者來勘，翚曰：「祖制，民墾荒田，永不科稅，奈何奪之？

translations.literal: When a ministry envoy came to survey, Hui said: "By ancestral institution, land the people reclaim from wasteland is never taxed—how can it be seized?"
translations.idiomatic: When a ministry envoy came to survey, Hui said, "By ancestral institution, land the people reclaim from wasteland is never taxed—how can it be seized?"

sentences.zh: 」使者奏如言，乃免。

translations.literal: " The envoy memorialized as Hui had said, and the seizure was waived.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy memorialized as Hui had said, and the seizure was waived.

sentences.zh: 成化初，轉左。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he was transferred to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chenghua he was transferred to the left post.

sentences.zh: 河南歲饑，計開封積粟多，奏請平糶，貧民賴以濟。

translations.literal: Henan suffered famine year after year; calculating that Kaifeng had much stored grain, he memorialized to sell at fair price, and the poor relied on it for relief.
translations.idiomatic: With famine in Henan year after year, noting that Kaifeng had much stored grain, he memorialized to sell at fair price and the poor were saved.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部左侍郎，仍食從二品俸。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, still drawing salary of the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments, still drawing salary of the second rank.

sentences.zh: 尋巡視浙江，考察官吏，奏罷不職者百余人，他弊政多所厘革。

translations.literal: Soon he inspected Zhejiang, examined officials, memorialized to dismiss more than a hundred who were derelict, and reformed many other abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he inspected Zhejiang, examined officials, memorialized to dismiss more than a hundred who were derelict, and reformed many other abuses.

sentences.zh: 還朝，久之，謝病去。

translations.literal: Returning to court, after a long time he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court, after a long time he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 翚操行謹，所至有聲。

translations.literal: Hui's conduct was careful; wherever he went he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's conduct was careful; wherever he went he won renown.

sentences.zh: 及歸，生計蕭然，絕跡公府，鄉人以為賢。

translations.literal: When he returned home his livelihood was bare; he never set foot in official mansions, and his fellow townsmen considered him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home his livelihood was bare; he never set foot in official mansions, and his fellow townsmen considered him worthy.

sentences.zh: 賈銓，字秉鈞，邯鄣人。

translations.literal: Jia Quan, styled Bingjun, was a man of Handan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Quan, whose style was Bingjun, came from Handan.

sentences.zh: 永樂末進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi at the end of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations at the end of the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年授禮科給事中，數有參駁。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites and several times submitted impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4 (1429) he was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites and several times submitted impeachments.

sentences.zh: 英宗踐阼，既肆赦，復命讞在京重囚，多所原宥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, after a general amnesty he again ordered review of serious prisoners in the capital, and many were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong took the throne, after a general amnesty he again ordered review of serious prisoners in the capital, and many were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 從銓請，推之南京。

translations.literal: At Quan's request this was extended to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At Quan's request this was extended to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，出為大理知府。

translations.literal: When his term ended he went out as prefect of Dali.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he went out as prefect of Dali.

sentences.zh: 王驥征麓川，饋運有勞。

translations.literal: When Wang Ji campaigned against Luchuan, Quan had merit in supplying transport.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ji campaigned against Luchuan, Quan had merit in supplying transport.

sentences.zh: 驥薦之。

translations.literal: Ji recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji recommended him.

sentences.zh: 麓川平，擢雲南左參政，仍知府事。

translations.literal: When Luchuan was pacified he was raised to left administration vice commissioner of Yunnan while still serving as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Luchuan was pacified he was raised to left administration vice commissioner of Yunnan while still serving as prefect.

sentences.zh: 尋以驥言，還治司事。

translations.literal: Soon, on Ji's word, he returned to manage the provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on Ji's word, he returned to manage the provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 正統十二年，左布政使闕，軍民數萬人頌銓，參贊軍務侍郎侯琎等亦疏請，銓遂得擢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengtong the left administration commissioner post was vacant; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians praised Quan, and military affairs vice minister Hou Jin and others also memorialized requesting him, and Quan was promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 12 (1447) the left administration commissioner post was vacant; tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians praised Quan, and military affairs vice minister Hou Jin and others also memorialized for him, and Quan was promoted.

sentences.zh: 土官十余部，歲當貢馬輸差發銀及海<貝巴>，八府民歲當輸食鹽米鈔。

translations.literal: More than ten native offices each year owed tribute horses, corvée silver, and sea cowries, and the people of the eight prefectures each year owed grain, salt, and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten native offices each year owed tribute horses, corvée silver, and sea cowries, and the people of the eight prefectures each year owed grain, salt, and paper money.

sentences.zh: 至景泰初，皆積逋不能償。

translations.literal: By the start of Jingtai all had accumulated arrears they could not pay.
translations.idiomatic: By the start of Jingtai all had accumulated arrears they could not pay.

sentences.zh: 銓等為言除之。

translations.literal: Quan and others memorialized to remit them.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and others memorialized to remit them.

sentences.zh: 治行聞，賜誥旌異。

translations.literal: His administration was renowned; he was granted an edict of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was renowned; he was granted an edict of commendation.

sentences.zh: 景泰七年，九載滿，當入都，軍民乞留。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jingtai, when nine years in office were complete and he should enter the capital, soldiers and civilians begged that he remain.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 7 (1456), when nine years in office were complete and he should enter the capital, soldiers and civilians begged that he remain.

sentences.zh: 命還任。

translations.literal: He was ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 天順四年與梁楘等舉政績卓異。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun he, with Liang You and others, was cited for outstanding achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 4 (1460) he, with Liang You and others, was cited for outstanding achievement.

sentences.zh: 戶部初闕尚書，王翺欲擢銓。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue first lacked a minister, Wang Ao wished to promote Quan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue first lacked a minister, Wang Ao wished to promote Quan.

sentences.zh: 帝問李賢，賢曰：「聞其名，未見其人也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Li Xian; Xian said: "I have heard his name but have not seen the man."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Li Xian; Xian said, "I have heard his name but have not seen the man."

sentences.zh: 」及是來覲，帝命賢視之，還奏貌寢。

translations.literal: " When Quan came to audience on this occasion, the Emperor ordered Xian to observe him; returning, Xian reported that his appearance was unprepossessing.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan came to audience on this occasion, the Emperor ordered Xian to observe him; returning, Xian reported that his appearance was unprepossessing.

sentences.zh: 乃以為右副都御史巡撫山東，尋兼撫河南。

translations.literal: He was therefore made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shandong and soon also grand coordinator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shandong and soon also grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 山東歲侵，請召還清軍御史。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered invasion that year; he asked that the investigating censors clearing troops be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong suffered invasion that year; he asked that the investigating censors clearing troops be recalled.

sentences.zh: 河南饑，請停征課馬。

translations.literal: Henan suffered famine; he asked that the levy of tribute horses be halted.
translations.idiomatic: Henan suffered famine; he asked that the levy of tribute horses be halted.

sentences.zh: 皆許之。

translations.literal: Both were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Both were granted.

sentences.zh: 成化初，左都御史李秉督師遼東，召銓署院事。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua, when left censor-in-chief Li Bing directed troops in Liaodong, Quan was summoned to act at the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chenghua, when left censor-in-chief Li Bing directed troops in Liaodong, Quan was summoned to act at the censorate.

sentences.zh: 中官唐慎等從征荊、襄還，杖死淮安知事谷淵，自奏丐免。

translations.literal: The eunuch Tang Shen and others, returning from campaigning in Jing and Xiang, beat to death Gu Yuan, an official of Huai'an, and memorialized asking to be excused.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tang Shen and others, returning from campaigning in Jing and Xiang, beat to death Gu Yuan, an official of Huai'an, and memorialized asking to be excused.

sentences.zh: 銓請罪之。

translations.literal: Quan asked that they be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Quan asked that they be punished.

sentences.zh: 乃付慎等司禮監，命法司罪其從人。

translations.literal: They were handed over to the Directorate of Ceremonial, and the law officers were ordered to punish their followers.
translations.idiomatic: They were handed over to the Directorate of Ceremonial, and the law officers were ordered to punish their followers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in office.

sentences.zh: 謚恭靖。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 銓在雲南，治行為一時冠。

translations.literal: Quan in Yunnan had administration that was the finest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan Quan's administration was the finest of the age.

sentences.zh: 比為巡撫，清靜不自表暴，吏民亦安之。

translations.literal: When he became grand coordinator he was quiet and did not display himself, and officials and people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator he was quiet and did not display himself, and officials and people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 王宇，字仲宏，祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu, styled Zhonghong, was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu, whose style was Zhonghong, came from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 童丱時，日記萬言，巡撫侍郎于謙奇之。

translations.literal: Even as a child he could memorize ten thousand characters a day; Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Yu Qian marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he could memorize ten thousand characters a day; Grand Coordinator Vice Minister Yu Qian marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 登正統四年進士，授南京戶部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Zhengtong and was appointed principal clerk of the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Zhengtong 4 (1439) and was appointed a principal clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 秩滿當轉郎中，吏部以宇才，特用為撫州知府。

translations.literal: When his term ended he should have been transferred to director, but the Ministry of Personnel, because of Yu's talent, specially appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he should have been transferred to director, but the Ministry of Personnel, valuing Yu's talent, specially appointed him prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 為政簡靜，而鋤強遏奸，凜不可犯，一府大治。

translations.literal: His government was simple and quiet, yet he rooted out the strong and checked the wicked; his authority was formidable and the whole prefecture was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was simple and quiet, yet he rooted out the strong and checked the wicked; his authority was formidable and the whole prefecture was greatly ordered.

sentences.zh: 天順元年，所司上其治行，詔賜誥命。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun the relevant office reported his administration; an edict granted him patent of appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 (1457) the relevant office reported his administration; an edict granted him a patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢山東右布政使，命撫恤所屬饑民。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised to right administration commissioner of Shandong and ordered to comfort and relieve famine victims in his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was raised to right administration commissioner of Shandong and ordered to comfort and relieve famine victims in his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 明年遷右副都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 中官嚴順、都督張林等令家人承納芻糧。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yan Shun and Commissioner-in-chief Zhang Lin and others had their households receive fodder and grain in their stead.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yan Shun and Commissioner-in-chief Zhang Lin and others had their households receive fodder and grain in their stead.

sentences.zh: 宇劾奏。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized and impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized and impeached them.

sentences.zh: 都御史寇深為解，帝切責深。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Kou Shen spoke in their defense; the Emperor sharply rebuked Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Kou Shen spoke in their defense; the Emperor sharply rebuked Shen.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼撫大同。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered also to grand-coordinate Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered also to grand-coordinate Datong.

sentences.zh: 石亨及從子彪驕恣，大同其舊鎮地，征索尤橫。

translations.literal: Shi Heng and his nephew Biao were arrogant and willful; Datong was their old command, and their exactions were especially overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Heng and his nephew Biao were arrogant and willful; Datong was their old command, and their exactions were especially overbearing.

sentences.zh: 宇抗疏論其奸，乞置之法。

translations.literal: Yu submitted a forthright memorial on their wickedness and begged that they be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Yu submitted a forthright memorial on their wickedness and begged that they be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不行，聞者敬憚。

translations.literal: Although the memorial was not acted on, those who heard of it respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Although the memorial was not acted on, those who heard of it respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 督餉郎中楊益不能備芻槁，為宇所劾。

translations.literal: Grain-supplying director Yang Yi could not provide sufficient fodder and was impeached by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Grain-supplying director Yang Yi could not provide sufficient fodder and was impeached by Yu.

sentences.zh: 戶部庇之，宇並劾尚書沈固等。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue shielded him; Yu also impeached Minister Shen Gu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue shielded him; Yu also impeached Minister Shen Gu and the others.

sentences.zh: 皆輸罪。

translations.literal: All admitted guilt.
translations.idiomatic: All admitted guilt.

sentences.zh: 遭喪，起復為大理卿。

translations.literal: On mourning he was recalled to serve as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: On mourning he was recalled to serve as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 宇剛介，所至有盛名。

translations.literal: Yu was upright and unyielding; wherever he went he had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was upright and unyielding; wherever he went he had a great reputation.

sentences.zh: 居大理，平反為多。

translations.literal: At the Court of Judicial Review he reversed many wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: At the Court of Judicial Review he reversed many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 七年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 崔恭，字克讓，廣宗人。

translations.literal: Cui Gong, styled Kerang, was a man of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong, whose style was Kerang, came from Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 正統元年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the first year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Zhengtong 1 (1436).

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出理延綏倉儲，有能聲。

translations.literal: He went out to manage Yan-sui grain stores and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to manage Yan-sui grain stores and had a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 以楊溥薦，擢萊州知府。

translations.literal: On Yang Pu's recommendation he was raised to prefect of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Yang Pu's recommendation he was raised to prefect of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 內地輸遼東布，悉貯郡庫，歲久朽敝，守者多破家。

translations.literal: Cloth for Liaodong levied from the interior was all stored in the prefectural treasury; after many years it rotted, and many custodians were ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Cloth for Liaodong levied from the interior was all stored in the prefectural treasury; after many years it rotted, and many custodians were ruined.

sentences.zh: 恭別構屋三十楹貯之，請約計歲輸外，余以充本府軍餉，遂放遣守者八百人。

translations.literal: Gong separately built thirty bays of housing to store it and asked that beyond the annual quota the surplus be used for the prefecture's military rations, then releasing eight hundred custodians.
translations.idiomatic: Gong separately built thirty bays of housing to store it and asked that beyond the annual quota the surplus be used for the prefecture's military rations, then releasing eight hundred custodians.

sentences.zh: 也先犯京師，遣民兵數千入援。

translations.literal: When Esen invaded the capital region, he sent several thousand militia to aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen invaded the capital region, he sent several thousand militia to aid.

sentences.zh: 廷議城臨清，檄發役夫。

translations.literal: The court debated fortifying Linqing and issued orders to levy laborers.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated fortifying Linqing and issued orders to levy laborers.

sentences.zh: 恭以方春民乏食，請俟秋成。

translations.literal: Gong, because in spring the people lacked food, asked to wait until the autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, because in spring the people lacked food, asked to wait until the autumn harvest.

sentences.zh: 居府六年，萊人以比漢楊震。

translations.literal: After six years in the prefecture, the people of Laizhou compared him to Han Yang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in the prefecture, the people of Laizhou compared him to Han Yang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，超遷湖廣右布政使。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai reign he was promoted over the regular steps to right administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingtai reign he was promoted over the regular steps to right administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 諸司供給，率取之民。

translations.literal: The various offices' supplies were generally taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: The various offices' supplies were generally taken from the people.

sentences.zh: 恭與僚佐約，悉罷之。

translations.literal: Gong agreed with his colleagues to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gong agreed with his colleagues to abolish them all.

sentences.zh: 公安、監利流民擅相殺。

translations.literal: Displaced people in Gong'an and Jianli killed one another at will.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people in Gong'an and Jianli killed one another at will.

sentences.zh: 恭下令願附籍者聽，否則迨秋遣歸，眾遂定。

translations.literal: Gong ordered that those willing to register might do so; otherwise they would be sent home in autumn, and the crowd was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gong ordered that those willing to register might do so; otherwise they would be sent home in autumn, and the crowd was settled.

sentences.zh: 尋遷江西左布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to left administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to left administration commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 司有廣濟庫，官吏幹沒五十萬。

translations.literal: The office had the Guangji treasury; officials embezzled five hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The office had the Guangji treasury; officials embezzled five hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 恭白於巡撫韓雍，典守者鹹獲罪。

translations.literal: Gong reported to Grand Coordinator Han Yong; all those in charge were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Gong reported to Grand Coordinator Han Yong; all those in charge were punished.

sentences.zh: 定均徭法，酌輕重，十年一役，遂為定例。

translations.literal: He fixed the equal-corvée law, weighing light and heavy, with one rotation every ten years, and it became the established rule.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the equal-corvée law, weighing light and heavy, with one rotation every ten years, and it became the established rule.

sentences.zh: 天順二年，寧王奠培不法，恭劾之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianshun the Prince of Ning, Mo Pei, acted unlawfully; Gong impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 2 (1458) the Prince of Ning, Mo Pei, acted unlawfully; Gong impeached him.

sentences.zh: 削其護衛，王稍戢。

translations.literal: His guard was reduced; the prince somewhat restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: His guard was reduced; the prince somewhat restrained himself.

sentences.zh: 遷右副都御史，代李秉巡撫蘇、松諸府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice censor-in-chief, replacing Li Bing as grand coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right vice censor-in-chief, replacing Li Bing as grand coordinator of Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 按部，進耆老言利病，為興革。

translations.literal: On inspecting his jurisdiction he advanced elders to speak of benefits and harms and instituted reforms.
translations.idiomatic: On inspecting his jurisdiction he brought forward elders to speak of benefits and harms and instituted reforms.

sentences.zh: 與都督徐恭浚儀真漕河，又浚常、鎮河，避江險。

translations.literal: Together with Commissioner-in-chief Xu Gong he dredged the Yizhen grain canal and also dredged the Chang and Zhen rivers to avoid the dangers of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: With Commissioner-in-chief Xu Gong he dredged the Yizhen grain canal and the Chang and Zhen rivers to avoid Yangzi hazards.

sentences.zh: 已，大治吳淞江。

translations.literal: Thereafter he greatly repaired the Wusong River.
translations.idiomatic: He then undertook a major repair of the Wusong River.

sentences.zh: 起昆山夏界口，至上海白鶴江，又自白鶴江至嘉定卞家渡，迄莊家涇，凡浚萬四千二百余丈。

translations.literal: From the Xiakou boundary of Kunshan to Baihe River at Shanghai, and from Baihe River to Bianjiadu in Jiading, reaching Zhuangjia Creek—in all more than fourteen thousand two hundred zhang were dredged.
translations.idiomatic: From Kunshan's Xiakou boundary to Baihe River at Shanghai, and from Baihe River to Bianjiadu in Jiading, reaching Zhuangjia Creek—more than fourteen thousand two hundred zhang were dredged in all.

sentences.zh: 又浚曹家港、蒲匯塘、新涇諸水。

translations.literal: He also dredged Caojia Harbor, Puhui Creek, Xinjing, and other waterways.
translations.idiomatic: He also dredged Caojia Harbor, Puhui Creek, Xinjing, and other waterways.

sentences.zh: 民賴其利，目曹家港為「都堂浦」。

translations.literal: The people relied on the benefit and called Caojia Harbor "Grand Coordinator Creek."
translations.idiomatic: The people benefited and called Caojia Harbor "Grand Coordinator Creek."

sentences.zh: 初，周忱奏定耗羨則例，李秉改定以賦之輕重遞盈縮。

translations.literal: At first Zhou Chen had memorialized fixed rules for surplus and loss; Li Bing had revised them to increase or decrease according to the lightness or heaviness of the tax.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhou Chen had fixed rules for surplus and loss; Li Bing had revised them to vary with the weight of each assessment.

sentences.zh: 其例甚平，而難於稽算，吏不勝煩擾。

translations.literal: The rules were very fair but hard to calculate; clerks could not bear the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The rules were fair but hard to calculate; clerks were overwhelmed.

sentences.zh: 恭乃罷去，悉如忱舊。

translations.literal: Gong then abolished them and restored Chen's old rules entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Gong abolished them and restored Chen's old rules entirely.

sentences.zh: 吏部缺右侍郎，李賢、王翺舉恭。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel lacked a right vice minister; Li Xian and Wang Ao recommended Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel lacked a right vice minister; Li Xian and Wang Ao recommended Gong.

sentences.zh: 遂召用。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed.

sentences.zh: 置「勸懲簿」，有聞皆識之。
