translations.literal: He kept a "Encouragement and Punishment Register" and recorded everything he heard.
translations.idiomatic: He kept an "Encouragement and Punishment Register" and recorded everything he heard.

sentences.zh: 翺甚倚恭，轉左。

translations.literal: Ao relied greatly on Gong and transferred him to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: Ao relied greatly on Gong and transferred him to the left post.

sentences.zh: 父憂起復。

translations.literal: On his father's death he was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he was recalled from mourning.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，乞致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong took the throne he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne he begged to retire.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted.

sentences.zh: 成化五年，尚書李秉罷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chenghua Minister Li Bing was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 5 (1469) Minister Li Bing was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 商輅欲用姚夔，彭時欲用王概，而北人居言路者，謂時實逐秉，喧謗於朝。

translations.literal: Shang Lu wished to use Yao Kui; Peng Shi wished to use Wang Gai; but northerners in the remonstrance offices said Shi had in fact driven Bing out and clamored at court.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Lu wished to use Yao Kui; Peng Shi wished to use Wang Gai; but northerners in the remonstrance offices said Shi had driven Bing out and clamored at court.

sentences.zh: 時稱疾不出，侍讀尹直以時、概皆已鄉人，恐因此得罪，急言於輅，以恭代秉。

translations.literal: Shi claimed illness and did not appear; Reader-in-waiting Yin Zhi, because Shi and Gai were both his fellow townsmen and feared they would be implicated, urgently spoke to Lu to have Gong replace Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Shi claimed illness and stayed away; Reader-in-waiting Yin Zhi, fearing Shi and Gai would be implicated as fellow townsmen, urgently persuaded Lu to have Gong replace Bing.

sentences.zh: 越五月，母喪歸。

translations.literal: After five months his mother died and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Five months later his mother died and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 服除，起南京吏部，劾罷諸司不識者數人。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and impeached several incompetent officials in the various offices.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel and impeached several incompetent officials.

sentences.zh: 十一年春命參贊機務。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was ordered to participate in deliberating state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was ordered to participate in deliberating state affairs.

sentences.zh: 居三年，致仕。

translations.literal: After three years he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he retired.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚莊敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 劉孜，字顯孜，萬安人。

translations.literal: Liu Zi, styled Xianzi, was a man of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zi, whose style was Xianzi, came from Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Zhengtong 10 (1445).

sentences.zh: 授御史，出按遼東。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and went out to inspect Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and sent to inspect Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 景帝即位，有建南遷議者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi took the throne, some proposed moving the capital south.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingdi took the throne, some proposed moving the capital south.

sentences.zh: 孜馳奏，乞斬言者以定人心。

translations.literal: Zi memorialized by express relay begging that those who spoke be executed to settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zi memorialized by express relay begging that the advocates be executed to settle people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 期滿當代，朝議邊務方殷，復留一歲。

translations.literal: When his term should have ended, the court debated that frontier affairs were pressing and kept him one more year.
translations.idiomatic: When his term should have ended, the court held that frontier affairs were pressing and kept him one more year.

sentences.zh: 再按畿輔。

translations.literal: He inspected the capital region a second time.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the capital region again.

sentences.zh: 時方築淪州城，以孜言罷。

translations.literal: At the time Lunzhou city was being built; on Zi's word it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Lunzhou city was being built; on Zi's word it was halted.

sentences.zh: 擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: He was raised to surveillance commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Shandong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天順四年，吏部舉天下治行卓異，按察使惟孜一人，遷左布政使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianshun the Ministry of Personnel cited outstanding administration throughout the realm; among surveillance commissioners only Zi was named, and he was transferred to left administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 4 (1460) the Ministry of Personnel cited outstanding administration; among surveillance commissioners only Zi was named, and he was made left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年春，以右副都御史巡撫江南十府。

translations.literal: In the spring of the following year he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of the ten prefectures of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Jiangnan's ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松財賦，自周忱立法後，代者多紛更。

translations.literal: The finances of Suzhou and Songjiang, since Zhou Chen had established the law, had been frequently changed by successive holders.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Songjiang finances, since Zhou Chen's law, had been frequently changed by successive holders.

sentences.zh: 孜首訪忱遺積，斟酌行之，民稱便。

translations.literal: Zi first sought out Chen's surviving rules, weighed and applied them, and the people said it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zi first sought Chen's surviving rules, weighed and applied them, and the people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，應天饑，方振貸，而江北饑民就食者眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, Yingtian suffered famine; relief was just beginning when famine refugees from north of the river came in great numbers to seek food.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 1 (1465), Yingtian suffered famine; relief had just begun when refugees from north of the river came in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 孜請盡發諸縣廩，全活無算。

translations.literal: Zi asked to release all the granaries of the various counties; innumerable lives were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Zi asked to open all county granaries; innumerable lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 時民間多積困：瀕江官田久廢沒，仍責輸賦；

translations.literal: At the time the people suffered many accumulated hardships: long-abandoned official fields along the river still had tax levied;
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered many accumulated hardships: long-abandoned riverside official fields still had tax levied;

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、杭、嘉諸府僉補富戶；

translations.literal: the prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, and Jiaxing conscripted wealthy households to make up shortfalls;
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou, Songjiang, Hangzhou, and Jiaxing conscripted wealthy households to make up shortfalls;

sentences.zh: 南京廊房既傾圮，猶征鈔；

translations.literal: Nanjing corridor shops had collapsed yet paper-money tax was still levied;
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing corridor shops had collapsed yet paper-money tax was still levied;

sentences.zh: 上元、江寧農民代河泊所綱戶采鰣魚；

translations.literal: farmers of Shangyuan and Jiangning were made to gather shad for river-boat households;
translations.idiomatic: Shangyuan and Jiangning farmers were made to gather shad for river-boat households;

sentences.zh: 應天都稅宣課諸司額外增稅；

translations.literal: the tax-supervising offices of Yingtian levied extra taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Yingtian tax offices levied extra taxes;

sentences.zh: 江陰諸縣民戶償納荒租；

translations.literal: households of Jiangyin and other counties repaid abandoned-land rents;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin and other counties' households repaid abandoned-land rents;

sentences.zh: 六合、江浦官牛歲征犢。

translations.literal: Liuhe and Jiangpu levied yearly calf taxes on official oxen.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe and Jiangpu levied yearly calf taxes on official oxen.

sentences.zh: 孜皆疏罷之。

translations.literal: Zi memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zi memorialized to abolish them all.

sentences.zh: 召拜南京刑部尚書，以宋傑代。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; Song Jie replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; Song Jie replaced him.

sentences.zh: 四年致仕，道卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he retired and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 孜廉慎，治事精審。

translations.literal: Zi was honest and careful and handled affairs with precision.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was honest and careful and handled affairs with precision.

sentences.zh: 然持法過嚴，時議其刻。

translations.literal: Yet he applied the law too strictly and contemporaries criticized him as harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he applied the law too strictly and contemporaries called him harsh.

sentences.zh: 傑為人長者。

translations.literal: Jie was a man of generous character.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was a man of generous character.

sentences.zh: 居二年，罷去，而邢宥代。

translations.literal: After two years he was dismissed and Xing You replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was dismissed and Xing You replaced him.

sentences.zh: 宥，文昌人。

translations.literal: You was a man of Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: You came from Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 正統十三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Zhengtong 13 (1448).

sentences.zh: 授御史，出巡福建。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and went out to inspect Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and sent to inspect Fujian.

sentences.zh: 民十人被誣為盜，當刑呼冤。

translations.literal: Ten people were falsely accused as bandits and were about to be executed when they cried out their innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Ten people were falsely accused as bandits and were about to be executed when they cried out their innocence.

sentences.zh: 宥為緩之，果得真盜。

translations.literal: You delayed the case and indeed found the real bandits.
translations.idiomatic: You delayed the case and found the real bandits.

sentences.zh: 天順中，出為臺州知府，有治績。

translations.literal: In the Tianshun reign he went out as prefect of Taizhou and had achievements in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshun reign he went out as prefect of Taizhou with solid achievements.

sentences.zh: 坐累謫晉江丞。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he was demoted assistant magistrate of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Through implication in a case he was demoted assistant magistrate of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗復其職，改知蘇州。

translations.literal: When Xianzong restored his post he was changed to prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong restored his post he was made prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 奸民攬納秋賦，置之法，得其贓萬緡，以隄沙河，甓官道。

translations.literal: Wicked men who collected autumn tax payments were punished by law; ten thousand strings of illicit gains were obtained and used to dike the Sha River and pave the official road.
translations.idiomatic: Tax-collecting bullies were punished by law; ten thousand strings of illicit gains were used to dike the Sha River and pave the official road.

sentences.zh: 大水，民饑，不待奏輒發米二十萬斛以振。

translations.literal: In great flood the people starved; without waiting for memorial he released two hundred thousand piculs of rice for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In great flood the people starved; without waiting for approval he released two hundred thousand piculs of rice for relief.

sentences.zh: 宥素廉介，及治蘇，嚴而不苛。

translations.literal: You had always been honest and upright; in governing Suzhou he was strict but not harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Always honest and upright, in governing Suzhou he was strict but not harsh.

sentences.zh: 傑薦於朝，詔加浙江左參政仍理府事，賜璽書。

translations.literal: Jie recommended him at court; an edict added him Zhejiang left administration vice commissioner while still managing the prefecture and granted an imperial letter.
translations.idiomatic: Jie recommended him; an edict made him Zhejiang left administration vice commissioner while still managing the prefecture and granted an imperial letter.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，遂以右僉都御史代傑巡撫。

translations.literal: After half a year he was made right vice censor-in-chief to replace Jie as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year he was made right vice censor-in-chief to replace Jie as grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 開丹陽河，築奔牛閘，省兌運冗費，民以為便。

translations.literal: He opened the Danyang River and built the Benniu sluice, saving redundant transport costs in grain exchange, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the Danyang River and built the Benniu sluice, saving redundant transport costs, and the people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 尋兼理兩浙鹽政，考察屬吏，奏黜不識者百七十余人。

translations.literal: Soon he also managed the salt administration of the two Zhe provinces, examined subordinates, and memorialized to dismiss more than one hundred and seventy incompetent men.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also managed the two Zhe salt administrations, examined subordinates, and dismissed more than one hundred and seventy incompetent men.

sentences.zh: 居數載，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After several years he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 李侃，字希正，東安人。

translations.literal: Li Kan, styled Xizheng, was a man of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kan, whose style was Xizheng, came from Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 正統七年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the seventh year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in Zhengtong 7 (1442).

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Revenue.

sentences.zh: 景帝監國，陳簡將才、募民壯、用戰車三事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi supervised the realm, he submitted three proposals: simplify military talent, recruit sturdy civilians, and use war chariots.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingdi supervised the realm, he submitted three proposals: simplify military talent, recruit sturdy civilians, and use war chariots.

sentences.zh: 也先逼京師議者欲焚城外馬草。

translations.literal: When Esen pressed on the capital some debated burning fodder outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Esen pressed on the capital some debated burning fodder outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 侃言敵輕剽，無持久心，乞勿焚，免復斂為民累。

translations.literal: Kan said the enemy were light raiders without staying power and begged that it not be burned, lest collection be repeated to the people's harm.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said the enemy were light raiders without staying power and begged that it not be burned, lest the people suffer renewed levies.

sentences.zh: 皆報許。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 時父母在容城，侃曉夜悲泣，乞假，冒險迎之。

translations.literal: At the time his parents were in Rongcheng; Kan wept day and night, begged leave, and braved danger to bring them away.
translations.idiomatic: His parents were in Rongcheng; Kan wept day and night, begged leave, and braved danger to bring them away.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，議錄扈從死事諸臣後。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingtai there was debate on recording posthumous honors for ministers who died escorting the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingtai there was debate on recording honors for ministers who died escorting the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 侃因言避難偷生者，宜嚴譴以厲臣節。

translations.literal: Kan said those who fled to escape disaster should be strictly punished to strengthen ministerial integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said those who fled should be strictly punished to strengthen ministerial integrity.

sentences.zh: 上皇將還，與同官劉福等言禮宜從厚。

translations.literal: When the Emperor on the northern campaign was about to return, he and his colleague Liu Fu and others spoke that the rites should be generous.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern Emperor was about to return, he and colleague Liu Fu said the rites should be generous.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，被詰，尚書胡濙為解，乃已。

translations.literal: This offended the throne and he was questioned; Minister Hu Ying explained and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the throne and he was questioned; Minister Hu Ying explained and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 再遷都給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to chief supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to chief supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 軍興，減天下學校師儒俸廩。

translations.literal: With military campaigns, salaries and grain rations of teachers in schools throughout the realm were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With military campaigns, salaries and grain of school teachers throughout the realm were reduced.

sentences.zh: 侃奏復之。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized to restore them.
translations.idiomatic: Kan memorialized to restore them.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書金濂違詔征租，侃論濂，下之吏。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Jin Lian violated an edict in collecting rent; Kan impeached Lian and sent him to the law officers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Lian violated an edict in collecting rent; Kan impeached him and sent him to the law officers.

sentences.zh: 石亨從子彪侵民業，侃請置重典，並嚴禁勛戚、中官不得豪奪細民，有司隱者同罪。

translations.literal: Shi Heng's nephew Biao encroached on people's property; Kan asked for heavy punishment and also strictly forbade nobles and eunuchs from seizing commoners' holdings, with officials who concealed this punished equally.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, nephew of Shi Heng, encroached on people's property; Kan asked heavy punishment and forbade nobles and eunuchs from seizing commoners' land, with concealing officials punished equally.

sentences.zh: 帝宥亨、彪，余如其請。

translations.literal: The Emperor pardoned Heng and Biao but granted the rest of his request.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pardoned Heng and Biao but granted the rest.

sentences.zh: 時給事中敢言者，林聰稱首，侃亦矯抗有直聲。

translations.literal: Among supervising secretaries who dared speak, Lin Cong was foremost; Kan also was upright and had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Among daring supervising secretaries Lin Cong was foremost; Kan also was upright with a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 廷議易儲，諸大臣唯唯。

translations.literal: At court they debated changing the heir; the great ministers assented one after another.
translations.idiomatic: At court they debated changing the heir; the great ministers assented one after another.

sentences.zh: 侃泣言東宮無失德，聰與御史朱英亦言不可，時議壯之。

translations.literal: Kan wept and said the Eastern Palace had not lost virtue; Cong and investigating censor Zhu Ying also said it could not be done, and contemporaries praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Kan wept that the heir had not lost virtue; Cong and censor Zhu Ying also objected, and contemporaries praised them.

sentences.zh: 擢詹事府丞。

translations.literal: He was raised to vice director of the Heir Apparent's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to vice director of the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 天順元年改太常丞，進太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 (1457) he was changed to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 明年復設山西巡撫，遷侃右僉都御史任之。

translations.literal: The following year the Shanxi grand coordinator was re-established and Kan was transferred as right vice censor-in-chief to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Shanxi grand coordinator was re-established and Kan was made right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「塞北之地，與窮荒無異。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The lands north of the passes are no different from utter wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Lands north of the passes are no different from utter wasteland.

sentences.zh: 非生長其間者，未有能寧居而狎敵者也。

translations.literal: Unless one grew up there, none could dwell at ease and be familiar with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one grew up there, none could dwell at ease or know the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今南人戍西北邊，怯風寒，聞寇股栗。

translations.literal: Now southerners garrison the northwest frontier, fear cold winds, and tremble at the mention of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Now southerners garrison the northwest, fear the cold, and tremble at bandits.

sentences.zh: 而北人戍南，亦不耐暑，多潛逃。

translations.literal: Northerners garrison the south cannot bear heat and mostly flee in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners garrison the south cannot bear heat and mostly flee in secret.

sentences.zh: 宜令南北清勾之軍，各就本土補伍，人情交便，戎備得修。

translations.literal: It is fitting that troops cleared north and south each fill vacancies in their native regions; feelings would be convenient and frontier defense would be maintained."
translations.idiomatic: Troops cleared north and south should each fill vacancies at home; feelings would be convenient and defense maintained."

sentences.zh: 」時不能用。

translations.literal: " At the time this could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 奏發巡按李傑罪，傑亦訐侃。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the crimes of inspecting censor Li Jie; Jie also accused Kan.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on inspecting censor Li Jie's crimes; Jie accused Kan in turn.

sentences.zh: 按傑事有驗，除名。

translations.literal: Investigation found Jie's case substantiated and he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation substantiated Jie's case and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 侃無贓罪，獲宥。

translations.literal: Kan had no corruption charge and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Kan had no corruption charge and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 六年考察屬吏，奏罷布政使王允、李正芳以下百六十人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he examined subordinates and memorialized to dismiss more than one hundred and sixty men including administration commissioners Wang Yun and Li Zhengfang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he examined subordinates and dismissed more than one hundred and sixty including commissioners Wang Yun and Li Zhengfang.

sentences.zh: 因言：「諸臣年與臣若、不堪任事者，臣悉退之，臣亦當罷。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ministers of my age or thereabouts who cannot perform their duties—I have all had them retire; I too should be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Ministers of my age who cannot perform their duties—I have had them retire; I too should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」詔不許。

translations.literal: " An edict did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict did not permit this.

sentences.zh: 侃性剛方，力振風紀，貪墨者屏跡。

translations.literal: Kan was upright and strove to restore discipline; the corrupt hid themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was upright and restored discipline; the corrupt hid themselves.

sentences.zh: 其年冬以母喪歸，軍民擁泣，至不得行。

translations.literal: That winter on his mother's death he returned home; soldiers and civilians wept and blocked his way so he could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: That winter on his mother's death he returned; soldiers and civilians wept and blocked his way so he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 服除，遂不出，家居十余年卒。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he never returned to office and died at home after more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he never returned and died at home after more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 侃事親孝，好學安貧，歿幾不能殮。

translations.literal: Kan was filial to his parents, loved learning, and was content in poverty; at death he almost could not be buried.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was filial, loved learning, and lived in poverty; at death he could barely afford burial.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，國子生江紀等言，前祭酒胡儼，都御史高明、李侃學行事功，彰著耳目，並乞賜謚。

translations.literal: At the start of Hongzhi, National University student Jiang Ji and others said that former Libationer Hu Yan, Censor-in-chief Gao Ming, and Li Kan had learning, conduct, and achievements plain to all, and begged posthumous titles.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Hongzhi, student Jiang Ji and others said former Libationer Hu Yan, Censor-in-chief Gao Ming, and Li Kan deserved posthumous titles.

sentences.zh: 寢不行。

translations.literal: The matter was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was shelved.

sentences.zh: 侃二子：德恢，嚴州知府；

translations.literal: Kan had two sons: Dekui, prefect of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Kan had two sons: Dekui, prefect of Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 德仁，河東鹽運使。

translations.literal: Deren, salt transport commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: and Deren, salt transport commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 雷復，字景昜，湖廣寧遠人。

translations.literal: Lei Fu, styled Jingyi, was a man of Ningyuan in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Fu, whose style was Jingyi, came from Ningyuan in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 正統初進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi at the start of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations at the start of Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 授行人，歷官廣西副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier and served as Guangxi vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed courier and served as Guangxi vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 藤縣民胡趙成構瑤陷縣治，復與參將範信討斬之。

translations.literal: Hu Zhaocheng of Teng county framed the Yao and seized the county seat; Fu, with participating general Fan Xin, campaigned and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zhaocheng of Teng county framed the Yao and seized the county; Fu, with general Fan Xin, campaigned and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 成化初以大臣會薦，擢山東右布政使。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua, on joint recommendation of great ministers, he was raised to right administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chenghua, on great ministers' joint recommendation, he was made right administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 七年征拜禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned and appointed right vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was summoned as right vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋改右副都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 繼李侃後，端恪守法，得軍民心。

translations.literal: Following Li Kan, he was upright and law-abiding and won the hearts of troops and people.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Kan, he was upright and law-abiding and won troops' and people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 敗寇紅沙煙，再敗之煙寺溝、石人村，賜敕獎勞。

translations.literal: He defeated bandits at Hongshayan and defeated them again at Yansi Ravine and Shiren Village; an imperial letter commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated bandits at Hongshayan and again at Yansi Ravine and Shiren Village; an imperial letter commended him.

sentences.zh: 時山西大浸，而廷議以陜西用兵，令預征芻餉，轉輸榆林。

translations.literal: At the time Shanxi suffered great flood while the court debated using troops in Shaanxi and ordered advance collection of fodder and provisions for transport to Yulin.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi suffered great flood while the court debated Shaanxi campaigns and ordered advance fodder collection for Yulin.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「自山西至榆林，道路險絕，民賫銀往易，價騰湧，不免稱貸，償責多破產。

translations.literal: Fu memorialized: "From Shanxi to Yulin the roads are perilous; the people carry silver to exchange and prices soar; they must borrow and many families are ruined paying debts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu memorialized, "From Shanxi to Yulin roads are perilous; people carry silver to buy grain at soaring prices and many families are ruined by debt.

sentences.zh: 今雨雪愆違，饑民疾病流離，困悴萬狀，而應輸綾帛、藥果諸物，又不下萬計。

translations.literal: Now rain and snow are untimely; famine victims are sick and displaced in every misery, yet silk, medicines, and fruits due still number no less than ten thousand items.
translations.idiomatic: Rain and snow are untimely; the sick and displaced suffer every misery, yet silk, medicines, and fruits due still number tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 乞依山東例蠲除，仍發帑振贍。

translations.literal: I beg remission following the Shandong precedent and treasury funds for relief."
translations.idiomatic: I beg remission following Shandong and treasury relief."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及發金三萬不足，請鬻鹽四十萬引，並令民入粟授散官。

translations.literal: When thirty thousand taels released proved insufficient, he asked to sell four hundred thousand salt certificates and let the people contribute grain for honorary offices.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand taels proved insufficient, he asked to sell four hundred thousand salt certificates and let people contribute grain for honorary offices.

sentences.zh: 皆報可。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 十年夏卒於官。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the tenth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 原傑，字子英，陽城人。

translations.literal: Yuan Jie, styled Ziying, was a man of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jie, whose style was Ziying, came from Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 正統十年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the tenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Zhengtong 10 (1445).

sentences.zh: 又二年，授南京御史，尋改北。

translations.literal: Two years later he was appointed Nanjing investigating censor and soon transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was made Nanjing investigating censor and soon transferred north.

sentences.zh: 巡按江西，捕誅劇盜，奸宄斂跡。

translations.literal: Inspecting Jiangxi he captured and executed major bandits and treachery subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting Jiangxi he captured major bandits and treachery subsided.

sentences.zh: 復按順天諸府。

translations.literal: He inspected Shuntian prefectures again.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected Shuntian prefectures again.

sentences.zh: 大水，牧官馬者乏芻，馬多斃，有司責償，傑請免之。

translations.literal: In great flood those tending official horses lacked fodder and many horses died; the relevant offices demanded compensation; Jie asked exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In great flood horse-keepers lacked fodder and many horses died; offices demanded compensation; Jie asked exemption.

sentences.zh: 開中鹽引入米振饑。

translations.literal: He opened middle-salt certificates to bring in grain for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: He opened middle-salt certificates to bring in grain for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 疏入，為部所格，景帝卒從傑議。

translations.literal: The memorial entered and was blocked by the ministry; Emperor Jingdi finally followed Jie's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry blocked it; Emperor Jingdi finally followed Jie's proposal.

sentences.zh: 超擢江西按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted over the regular steps to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted over the regular steps to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 發寧王奠培淫亂事，革其護衛。

translations.literal: He exposed the Prince of Ning Mo Pei's debauchery and reduced his guard.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Prince of Ning Mo Pei's debauchery and reduced his guard.

sentences.zh: 治行聞，賜誥旌異，遷山東左布政使。

translations.literal: His administration was renowned; he was granted an edict of commendation and transferred to left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was renowned; he received commendation and was made Shandong left administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化二年就拜右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he was immediately appointed right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator there.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 2 (1466) he was immediately made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator there.

sentences.zh: 歲兇振救，民無流移。

translations.literal: In famine years he gave relief and the people did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he gave relief and the people did not flee.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as left vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as left vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時黃河遷決不常，彼陷則此淤。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River shifted and breached unpredictably; where it sank one place silted another.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River shifted and breached unpredictably; where it sank one place silted another.

sentences.zh: 軍民就淤墾種。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians reclaimed and planted the silt.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians reclaimed the silt.

sentences.zh: 奸徒指為園場屯地，獻王府邀賞，王府輒據有之。

translations.literal: Scoundrels pointed to it as garden or garrison land, presented it to the princely establishment for reward, and the establishment seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Scoundrels called it garden or garrison land, presented it to the prince for reward, and the establishment seized it.

sentences.zh: 傑請獻者謫戍，並罪受獻者。

translations.literal: Jie asked that presenters be banished to garrison service and recipients also punished.
translations.idiomatic: Jie asked presenters be banished and recipients punished.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was granted.

sentences.zh: 江西盜起，以傑嘗再蒞其地得民，詔往治。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Jiangxi, because Jie had twice served there and won the people, an edict sent him to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi bandits rose, because Jie had twice won the people there, an edict sent him.

sentences.zh: 捕戮六百余人，余悉解散。

translations.literal: He captured and killed more than six hundred; the rest were all dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: He killed more than six hundred; the rest were dispersed.

sentences.zh: 改左副都御史，還佐院事。

translations.literal: He was changed to left vice censor-in-chief and returned to assist at the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left vice censor-in-chief and returned to assist the censorate.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄流民數十萬，朝廷以為憂。

translations.literal: Several hundred thousand displaced people in Jing and Xiang alarmed the court.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred thousand displaced people in Jing and Xiang alarmed the court.

sentences.zh: 祭酒周洪謨嘗著《流民圖說》，謂當增置府縣，聽附籍為編氓，可實襄、鄧戶口，俾數百年無患。

translations.literal: Libationer Zhou Hongmo had written "Illustrated Discourse on Displaced People," saying prefectures and counties should be added and they should be allowed to register as commoners to fill Xiang and Deng households and remove trouble for centuries.
translations.idiomatic: Libationer Zhou Hongmo's "Illustrated Discourse on Displaced People" urged new prefectures and counties and registration as commoners to fill Xiang and Deng and remove centuries of trouble.

sentences.zh: 都御史李賓以聞，帝善之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Li Bin reported this; the Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Bin reported it; the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遂命傑出撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Jie was ordered out to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Jie was ordered out to pacify.

sentences.zh: 遍歷山溪，宣朝廷德意，諸流民欣然願附籍。

translations.literal: Traversing mountains and streams he proclaimed the court's benevolence; the displaced gladly wished to register.
translations.idiomatic: Traversing mountains and streams he proclaimed the court's benevolence; the displaced gladly wished to register.

sentences.zh: 於是大會湖廣、河南、陜西撫、按官籍之，得戶十一萬三千有奇，口四十三萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he convened Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi grand coordinators and inspectors to register them, obtaining more than one hundred and thirteen thousand households and more than four hundred and thirty-eight thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: He convened Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi officials to register them: more than 113,000 households and 438,000 persons.

sentences.zh: 其初至，無產及平時頑梗者，驅還其鄉，而附籍者用輕則定田賦。

translations.literal: Those who had just arrived without property and those usually stubborn were sent back to their native places; registrants were given light land-tax assessments.
translations.idiomatic: Those without property and the stubborn were sent home; registrants received light land-tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 民大悅。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 因相地勢，以襄陽所轄鄖縣，居竹、房、上津、商、洛諸縣中，道路四達，去襄陽五百余裏。

translations.literal: Considering the terrain, Yun county under Xiangyang lay among Zhushan, Fang, Shangjin, Shang, Luo, and other counties, with roads in all directions, five hundred-odd li from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yun county under Xiangyang lay among Zhushan, Fang, Shangjin, Shang, Luo, and other counties, roads in all directions, five hundred-odd li from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 山林阻深，將吏鮮至，猝有盜賊，府難遙制。

translations.literal: Mountains and forests were deep; officers rarely came; sudden bandits were hard for the prefecture to control from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains were deep, officers rare; sudden bandits were hard to control from afar.

sentences.zh: 乃拓其城，置鄖陽府，以縣附之。

translations.literal: He therefore expanded the city and established Yunyang prefecture, attaching the county to it.
translations.idiomatic: He expanded the city and established Yunyang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 且置湖廣行都司，增兵設戍，而析竹山置竹溪，析鄖置鄖西，析漢中之洵陽置白河，與竹山、上津、房鹹隸新府。

translations.literal: He also established the Huguang regional military commission, increased troops and garrisons, split Zhushan to create Zhuxi, split Yun to create Yunxi, split Xunyang in Hanzhong to create Baihe, and attached Zhushan, Shangjin, and Fang to the new prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He established the Huguang regional military commission, increased garrisons, created Zhuxi, Yunxi, and Baihe, and attached Zhushan, Shangjin, and Fang to the new prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又於西安增山陽，南陽增南召、桐柏，汝州增伊陽，各隸其舊府。

translations.literal: He also added Shanyang in Xi'an, Nanzhao and Tongbai in Nanyang, and Yiyang in Ruzhou, each under its former prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He added Shanyang in Xi'an, Nanzhao and Tongbai in Nanyang, and Yiyang in Ruzhou under their former prefectures.

sentences.zh: 制既定，薦知鄧州吳遠為鄖陽知府，諸縣皆擇鄰境良吏為之。

translations.literal: When the system was set he recommended Wu Yuan, prefect of Dengzhou, as Yunyang prefect and chose good officials from neighboring jurisdictions for the counties.
translations.idiomatic: When the system was set he recommended Wu Yuan of Dengzhou as Yunyang prefect and chose good neighboring officials for the counties.

sentences.zh: 流人得所，四境乂安。

translations.literal: The displaced found places; the four borders were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced found places; the borders were at peace.

sentences.zh: 將還，以地界湖廣、河南、陜西，事無統紀，因薦御史吳道宏自代。

translations.literal: About to return, because the region bordered Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi and lacked unified oversight, he recommended investigating censor Wu Daohong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: About to return, because the region bordered three provinces without unified oversight, he recommended censor Wu Daohong to replace him.

sentences.zh: 詔即擢道宏大理少卿，撫治鄖陽、襄陽、荊州、南陽、西安、漢中六府。

translations.literal: An edict immediately raised Daohong to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review to pacify Yunyang, Xiangyang, Jingzhou, Nanyang, Xi'an, and Hanzhong's six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict raised Daohong to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review to pacify six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鄖陽之有撫治，自此始也。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioners for Yunyang began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yunyang pacification commissioners began from this.

sentences.zh: 傑以功進右都御史。

translations.literal: Jie was promoted to right censor-in-chief for his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was promoted to right censor-in-chief for his achievement.

sentences.zh: 傑數揚歷於外，既居內臺，不欲出。

translations.literal: Jie had often served outside; once in the inner censorate he did not wish to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Jie had often served outside; once in the capital censorate he did not wish to go out.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄之命，非其意也。

translations.literal: The Jing-Xiang appointment was not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: The Jing-Xiang appointment was not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 事竣，急請還朝。

translations.literal: When affairs ended he urgently asked to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs ended he urgently asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 會南京兵部缺尚書，以傑任之。

translations.literal: When the Nanjing Ministry of War lacked a minister, Jie was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing Ministry of War lacked a minister, Jie was appointed.

sentences.zh: 傑疏辭。

translations.literal: Jie memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Jie memorialized to decline.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 遂卒於南陽，年六十一。

translations.literal: He then died at Nanyang, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Nanyang, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 鄖、襄民為立祠，詔贈太子太保，錄其子宗敏為國子生。

translations.literal: The people of Yun and Xiang built shrines; an edict posthumously made him Grand Guardian and enrolled his son Zongmin in the National University.
translations.idiomatic: Yun and Xiang people built shrines; an edict posthumously made him Grand Guardian and enrolled his son Zongmin in the National University.

sentences.zh: 彭誼，字景宜，東莞人。

translations.literal: Peng Yi, styled Jingyi, was a man of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yi, whose style was Jingyi, came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 正統中，由鄉舉除工部司務。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong, through provincial recommendation he was made clerk of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong, through provincial recommendation he was made a Ministry of Works clerk.

sentences.zh: 嘗與尚書辯事，無所阿。

translations.literal: He once debated affairs with a minister and showed no flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He once debated affairs with a minister without flattery.

sentences.zh: 景帝立，用薦改御史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingdi took the throne, on recommendation he was changed to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingdi took the throne, on recommendation he was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 從尚書石璞塞沙灣決河，進秩二等。

translations.literal: Following Minister Shi Pu in blocking the Shawan breach on the Yellow River, he was advanced two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Following Minister Shi Pu in blocking the Shawan breach, he was advanced two ranks.

sentences.zh: 復決，再往塞之。

translations.literal: When it breached again he went again to block it.
translations.idiomatic: When it breached again he went again to block it.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年，以從大學士王文巡視江、淮，擒獲蘇州賊，擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingtai, following Grand Secretary Wang Wen in inspecting Jiang and Huai, he captured Suzhou bandits and was raised to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 5 (1454), following Wang Wen inspecting Jiang and Huai, he captured Suzhou bandits and was made Court of Judicial Review vice director.

sentences.zh: 時年二月擢右僉都御史，提督紫荊、倒馬諸關。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he was raised to right vice censor-in-chief directing Zijing, Daoma, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: That second month he was made right vice censor-in-chief directing Zijing, Daoma, and other passes.

sentences.zh: 劾都指揮胡璽納賄縱軍罪。

translations.literal: He impeached Commissioner-in-chief Hu Xi for taking bribes and indulging troops.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Commissioner-in-chief Hu Xi for bribes and indulging troops.

sentences.zh: 天順初，罷巡撫官。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshun, grand coordinator posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianshun, grand coordinator posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 中朝有不悅誼者，下遷紹興知府。

translations.literal: Someone at court disliked Yi and he was demoted prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Someone at court disliked Yi and he was demoted to Shaoxing prefect.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，輒發廩振貸。

translations.literal: In famine years he promptly opened granaries for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he promptly opened granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 吏白當俟朝命，誼曰：「民方急，安得循故事耶？

translations.literal: Clerks said they should await court orders; Yi said: "The people are in urgent need—how can we follow precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: Clerks said to await orders; Yi said, "The people are desperate—how can we follow precedent?"

sentences.zh: 」築白馬閘障海潮。

translations.literal: " He built the Baiyang sluice to block sea tides.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Baiyang sluice to block sea tides.

sentences.zh: 歷九載，多惠政。

translations.literal: Over nine years he had many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: Over nine years he had many benevolent policies.

sentences.zh: 超擢山東左布政使，入為工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted over the regular steps to Shandong left administration commissioner and entered as left vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Shandong left administration commissioner and entered as left vice minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 成化四年，遼東巡撫張岐得罪，吏部舉代者。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chenghua, Liaodong grand coordinator Zhang Qi offended and the Ministry of Personnel nominated a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 4 (1468), Liaodong grand coordinator Zhang Qi offended and the Ministry nominated a replacement.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「遼東自王翺後，屢更巡撫，多不稱，可於大臣中求之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Since Wang Ao in Liaodong, grand coordinators have been changed repeatedly and mostly failed; seek one among the great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Since Wang Ao, Liaodong grand coordinators have mostly failed; seek one among the great ministers."

sentences.zh: 」乃改誼右副都御史以往，鎮守中官橫征諸屬衛。

translations.literal: " Yi was therefore changed to right vice censor-in-chief and sent there; garrison eunuchs levied heavily on subordinate guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was made right vice censor-in-chief and sent there; garrison eunuchs levied heavily on the guards.

sentences.zh: 誼下令，凡文牒不經巡撫審定者，所司毋輒行，虐焰為息。

translations.literal: Yi ordered that no document not approved by the grand coordinator be acted on; oppressive exactions ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yi ordered that no document not approved by the grand coordinator be acted on; oppressive exactions ceased.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，戶部檄所司開黑山金場。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year the Ministry of Revenue ordered opening the Heishan gold fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year the Ministry ordered opening the Heishan gold fields.

sentences.zh: 誼奏永樂中太監王彥等開是山，督夫六千人，三閱月止得金八兩，請罷之。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized that in Yongle eunuch Wang Yan and others had opened that mountain, supervised six thousand laborers for three months, and obtained only eight taels of gold; he asked that it be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized that in Yongle eunuch Wang Yan had opened that mountain with six thousand laborers for three months and obtained only eight taels of gold; he asked that it stop.

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: It was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: It was stopped.

sentences.zh: 誼好古博學，通律歷、占象、水利、兵法之屬。

translations.literal: Yi loved antiquity and broad learning and was versed in calendrics, astrology, waterworks, and military science.
translations.idiomatic: Yi loved antiquity and broad learning and was versed in calendrics, astrology, waterworks, and military science.

sentences.zh: 平居謙厚簡默，臨事毅然有斷。

translations.literal: In daily life he was humble and quiet, but in affairs he was resolute and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he was humble and quiet, but in affairs resolute and decisive.

sentences.zh: 鎮遼八年，軍令振肅。

translations.literal: Garrisoning Liaodong eight years, military discipline was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisoning Liaodong eight years, he restored military discipline.

sentences.zh: 年未老，四疏告歸，家居四十余年卒。

translations.literal: Though not old, he memorialized four times to retire and died at home after more than forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Though not old, he memorialized four times to retire and died at home after more than forty years.

sentences.zh: 牟俸，巴人。

translations.literal: Mou Feng was a man of Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Feng came from Ba.

sentences.zh: 景泰初進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi at the start of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi at the start of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 授御史，巡按雲南。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor and inspected Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and inspected Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 南寧伯毛勝鎮金齒，俸列其違縱罪，將吏皆聳。

translations.literal: Nanning Earl Mao Sheng garrisoned Jinchí; Feng listed his violations and indulgence; officers were all awed.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning Earl Mao Sheng garrisoned Jinchí; Feng listed his violations; officers were awed.

sentences.zh: 天順元年出為福建僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun he went out as Fujian vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun 1 he went out as Fujian vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 成化初，進秩副使。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he was advanced in rank to vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Chenghua he was advanced to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷江西按察使，政尚嚴厲，入為太仆卿。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner; his government was stern; he entered as chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He became Jiangxi surveillance commissioner, governed sternly, and entered as chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 八年以左僉都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made left vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made left vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲祲，請發濟南倉儲減價以糶，令臨清關稅收米麥濟振。

translations.literal: In famine he asked to release Jinan granary stores at reduced price and use Linqing customs grain and wheat for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he asked to sell Jinan grain cheaply and use Linqing customs grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were granted.
translations.idiomatic: All were granted.

sentences.zh: 時大饑，雖獲振，饑民眾，轉徙益多。

translations.literal: At the time famine was severe; though relief was given, famine victims were many and displacement increased.
translations.idiomatic: Famine was severe; though relief was given, displacement increased.

sentences.zh: 俸請敕鄰境撫、按隨所在安輯，秋成資遣復業。

translations.literal: Feng asked an edict that neighboring grand coordinators and inspectors pacify people wherever they were and send them home after harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Feng asked neighboring officials pacify the displaced and send them home after harvest.

sentences.zh: 又乞開中淮、浙鹽百萬引，盡蠲州縣逋課。

translations.literal: He also begged to open middle-salt on Huai and Zhe for a million certificates and remit all prefectural arrears.
translations.idiomatic: He begged middle-salt on Huai and Zhe for a million certificates and full remission of arrears.

sentences.zh: 詔如所請，更命移臨清倉粟十萬石振之。

translations.literal: An edict granted as requested and additionally ordered ten thousand piculs moved from Linqing granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted this and ordered ten thousand piculs from Linqing for relief.

sentences.zh: 至七月，俸又言公私困竭，救荒靡策，乞開納粟例，令胥吏得就選，富民授散官，且截留漕糧備振。

translations.literal: By the seventh month Feng again said public and private resources were exhausted with no policy for famine relief; he begged to open grain-purchase offices, let clerks qualify for selection, grant wealthy men honorary offices, and retain grain transport for relief.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month Feng begged grain-purchase offices, clerk selection, honorary offices for the wealthy, and retained transport grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 十月復言：「今救荒者止救其饑，不謀其寒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he again said: "Today's relief only saves hunger, not cold.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he said, "Today's relief saves hunger, not cold.

sentences.zh: 縱得食，終不免僵死，乞貸貧民布棉。

translations.literal: Even with food they will freeze to death; I beg cloth and cotton on loan to the poor."
translations.idiomatic: Even with food they may freeze; I beg cloth and cotton on loan."

sentences.zh: 」帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: " The Emperor commended and adopted all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended and adopted all.

sentences.zh: 俸又檄發東昌、濟寧倉粟十萬余石為軍士月糧，而以德州、臨清寄庫銀易米振濟，奏請伏專擅罪。

translations.literal: Feng also ordered release of more than one hundred thousand piculs from Dongchang and Jining granaries for soldiers' monthly grain, exchanged deposited silver at Dezhou and Linqing for rice for relief, and memorialized asking to confess overstepping authority.
translations.idiomatic: Feng released granary grain for soldiers' rations, exchanged deposited silver for relief rice, and asked to confess overstepping authority.

sentences.zh: 帝特宥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 已，復以俸奏免柴夫折價銀，移河南輸邊粟濟山東，而別給銀為邊餉，山東輸京租二十萬石，給本地用。

translations.literal: Thereafter on Feng's memorial firewood-bearer commutation silver was remitted, Henan border grain was shifted to aid Shandong while silver was given for border pay, and Shandong's two hundred thousand piculs capital rent was kept for local use.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Feng won remission of firewood commutation, Henan grain for Shandong, and local retention of capital rent.

sentences.zh: 十年又饑，請發倉儲出貸。

translations.literal: In the tenth year famine came again; he asked to lend from granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year famine returned; he asked to lend from granaries.

sentences.zh: 撫山東五年，盡心荒政，活饑民不可勝數。

translations.literal: Grand-coordinating Shandong five years, he devoted himself to famine administration and saved countless starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Five years in Shandong he devoted himself to famine work and saved countless people.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史改撫蘇、松。

translations.literal: He was changed to right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 俸性嚴。

translations.literal: Feng was stern by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was stern by nature.

sentences.zh: 以所部多巨室，欲故摧抑之，乃禁索私租，勸富家出谷備振動千計，怨謗紛然。

translations.literal: Because his jurisdiction had many great families he wished to humble them; he forbade private rent collection and urged wealthy families to contribute grain for relief by the thousands; complaints arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: With many great families he forbade private rents and urged grain contributions; complaints arose.

sentences.zh: 中官汪直有事南京，或譖俸。

translations.literal: The eunuch Wang Zhi had business at Nanjing; some slandered Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch Wang Zhi had business at Nanjing; some slandered Feng.

sentences.zh: 直歸，未發也。

translations.literal: Zhi returned but had not yet acted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi returned but had not yet acted.

sentences.zh: 俸初在山東，與布政陳鉞負氣不相下。

translations.literal: Feng in Shandong had been mutually overbearing with administration commissioner Chen Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In Shandong Feng had clashed with commissioner Chen Yue.

sentences.zh: 後鉞從容言俸短，直信之。

translations.literal: Later Yue casually spoke of Feng's faults and Zhi believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yue spoke of Feng's faults and Zhi believed him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，俸議事至京，直請執俸下詔獄。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Feng came to the capital on business; Zhi asked that Feng be seized and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Feng came to the capital; Zhi had him seized for the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 先是，所親學士江朝宗除服還朝，俸迓之九江，聯舟並下。

translations.literal: Earlier, his intimate Academician Jiang Chaozong returned from mourning; Feng met him at Jiujiang and traveled downriver together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Academician Jiang Chaozong returned from mourning; Feng met him at Jiujiang and traveled together.

sentences.zh: 所至，有司供張頗盛。

translations.literal: Wherever they went local offices entertained them lavishly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they went local offices entertained them lavishly.

sentences.zh: 直因謂朝宗有所關說，並下獄。

translations.literal: Zhi therefore said Chaozong had lobbied for him; both were imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said Chaozong had lobbied; both were imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 詞連僉事吳扁等十余人，俱被逮。

translations.literal: The case implicated more than ten others including Vice Commissioner Wu Bian; all were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated Vice Commissioner Wu Bian and more than ten others.

sentences.zh: 系獄半歲，謫戍湖廣。

translations.literal: After half a year in prison they were banished to garrison service in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year they were banished to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 俸在江西時，共成許聰獄，人多議其深文。

translations.literal: In Jiangxi Feng had joined in the Xu Cong case; many criticized his harsh construction of charges.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi Feng had joined the Xu Cong case; many criticized his harsh charges.

sentences.zh: 至是被禍，皆知為直誣，然無白其冤者。

translations.literal: When disaster struck all knew it was Zhi's false charge, yet none cleared his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck all knew Zhi's false charge, yet none cleared him.

sentences.zh: 逾年，卒戍所。

translations.literal: After a year he died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 夏壎，字宗成，天臺人。

translations.literal: Xia Xun, styled Zongcheng, was a man of Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Xun, whose style was Zongcheng, came from Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the second year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jingtai 2 (1451).

sentences.zh: 授御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 天順初，巡按福建，繼清軍江西，發鎮守中官葉達恣橫狀，達為斂威。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshun he inspected Fujian, then cleared troops in Jiangxi, and exposed the garrison eunuch Ye Da's overbearing conduct; Da restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshun's start he inspected Fujian, cleared troops in Jiangxi, and exposed eunuch Ye Da; Da restrained himself.

sentences.zh: 以薦超擢廣東按察使。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was promoted over the regular steps to Guangdong surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was promoted to Guangdong surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時用師歲久，役民守城，壎至悉遣之。

translations.literal: Troops had been used for years; the people were conscripted to guard cities; when Xun arrived he sent them all home.
translations.idiomatic: Long campaigns had conscripted city guards; Xun sent them all home.

sentences.zh: 成化初，奏：「瑤、僮弗靖，用兵無功，由有司撫字乖方，賊因得誘良民為徒黨。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua he memorialized: "The Yao and Zhuang are unsettled; military campaigns fail because local officials govern badly and bandits lure good people into gangs.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenghua's start he memorialized, "Yao and Zhuang unrest fails because officials govern badly and bandits lure good people.

sentences.zh: 劇寇數百，脅從萬千，進則驅之當前，退則殺以抒憤，害常在民，而利常在彼。

translations.literal: Major bandits number only hundreds but coerce tens of thousands; advancing they drive them forward, retreating they kill to vent anger; harm always falls on the people while profit stays with them.
translations.idiomatic: Major bandits are hundreds but coerce tens of thousands; harm falls on the people while profit stays with bandits.

sentences.zh: 況用兵不已，供斂日增。

translations.literal: Moreover campaigns do not cease and levies increase daily.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns do not cease and levies increase daily.

sentences.zh: 以易搖之人心，責無窮之軍費。

translations.literal: With easily swayed hearts to meet endless military costs,
translations.idiomatic: With easily swayed hearts to meet endless military costs,

sentences.zh: 恐外患未除，內變先作。

translations.literal: I fear internal trouble will arise before external trouble is removed.
translations.idiomatic: I fear internal trouble before external trouble is removed.

sentences.zh: 請慎選監司守令，撫綏遺民，彼被脅之眾自聞風來歸。

translations.literal: Choose surveillance commissioners and prefects carefully, comfort the surviving people, and those coerced will return on hearing the news."
translations.idiomatic: Choose officials carefully, comfort survivors, and the coerced will return."

sentences.zh: 」帝深納其言。

translations.literal: " The Emperor deeply accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor deeply accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 尋遷布政使，調江西。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred administration commissioner and moved to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made administration commissioner and moved to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 八年以右副都御史巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 苗、僚時為寇。

translations.literal: Miao and Lao often raided.
translations.idiomatic: Miao and Lao often raided.

sentences.zh: 壎立互知會捕法，賊為之戢。

translations.literal: Xun established mutual-notification arrest laws and bandits were curbed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun established mutual-notification arrest laws and bandits were curbed.

sentences.zh: 古州苗萬余，居爛土久，時議逐之，壎謂非計。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand Miao of Guzhou had long lived on ruined land; some proposed expelling them; Xun said this was not the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Guzhou Miao lived on ruined land; expulsion was proposed; Xun objected.

sentences.zh: 松潘參將堯彧請益戍兵三千，又力陳不可。

translations.literal: Songpan participating general Yao Yu asked to add three thousand garrison troops; Xun again strongly argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: Songpan general Yao Yu asked three thousand more troops; Xun again objected.

sentences.zh: 皆得寢。

translations.literal: Both were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Both were shelved.

sentences.zh: 已，奏所部將校多犯法，奏請逾時，輒至遁逸。

translations.literal: Thereafter he memorialized that many officers in his jurisdiction broke the law and when memorials were delayed they fled.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized many officers broke the law and fled when memorials were delayed.

sentences.zh: 請先逮系，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: He asked to arrest first and report afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to arrest first and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 帝可之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 壎剛介，善聽斷，所至民不冤。

translations.literal: Xun was upright, skilled in hearing cases, and wherever he went the people were not wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was upright and skilled in judgment; the people were not wronged.

sentences.zh: 在蜀二年，民夷畏服。

translations.literal: In Shu two years, Chinese and tribes feared and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Two years in Shu, Chinese and tribes obeyed.

sentences.zh: 然厭繁劇，與時多齟齬。

translations.literal: Yet he disliked complexity and often clashed with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he disliked complexity and clashed with the times.

sentences.zh: 子堠獻詩勸歸，壎欣然納焉。

translations.literal: His son Yu presented a poem urging retirement and Xun gladly accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yu urged retirement in verse and Xun gladly accepted.

sentences.zh: 年未五十，即求退。

translations.literal: Not yet fifty, he sought to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Not yet fifty, he sought to retire.

sentences.zh: 章四上，得請。

translations.literal: Four memorials and he was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Four memorials and he was permitted.

sentences.zh: 既歸，杜門養親，不按賓客。

translations.literal: Once home he shut his door to nurture his parents and did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: Once home he shut his door to nurture his parents.

sentences.zh: 又五年卒。

translations.literal: Five years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died.

sentences.zh: 鍭，舉進士。

translations.literal: Yu passed the jinshi examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Yu passed the jinshi examinations.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年謁選入都，上書請復李文祥、鄒智等官，罷大學士劉吉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, awaiting selection in the capital, he memorialized asking restoration of Li Wenxiang, Zou Zhi, and others and dismissal of Grand Secretary Liu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 4 he memorialized to restore Li Wenxiang and Zou Zhi and dismiss Liu Ji.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，下獄，得釋。

translations.literal: This offended the throne; he was imprisoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: This offended the throne; he was imprisoned then released.

sentences.zh: 久之，除南京大理評事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made reviewing official of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Nanjing Court of Judicial Review reviewing official.

sentences.zh: 疏論賦斂、徭役、馬政、鹽課利弊及宗藩、戚裏侵漁狀。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the pros and cons of levies, corvée, horse policy, and salt tax and on encroachments by imperial clans and in-laws.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on levies, corvée, horses, salt, and encroachments by clans and in-laws.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: No response was given.

sentences.zh: 鍭素無宦情。

translations.literal: Yu had never desired office.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had never desired office.

sentences.zh: 居官僅歲餘，念母老，乞侍養，遂歸。

translations.literal: In office barely over a year, thinking his mother old, he begged to serve her and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In office barely a year he begged to serve his aged mother and returned.

sentences.zh: 家居三十余年，竟不復出。

translations.literal: At home more than thirty years he never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: At home more than thirty years he never came out again.

sentences.zh: 高明，字上達，貴溪人。

translations.literal: Gao Ming, styled Shangda, was a man of Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Ming, whose style was Shangda, came from Guixi.

sentences.zh: 幼事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: As a child he was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was known for filial service to his mother.

sentences.zh: 登景泰二年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in Jingtai 2 and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Jingtai 2 and was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 聞內苑造龍舟，切諫。

translations.literal: Hearing the inner park was building dragon boats, he remonstrated sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the inner park built dragon boats, he remonstrated sharply.

sentences.zh: 有指揮為大臣所陷，論死，辯出之。

translations.literal: A commander was framed by a great minister and sentenced to death; Ming argued and freed him.
translations.idiomatic: A commander was framed and sentenced to death; Ming freed him.

sentences.zh: 徐州民訴有司於朝，時例，越訴者戍邊。

translations.literal: Xuzhou people appealed against local officials at court; at the time the rule was that those who appealed across jurisdictions were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou people appealed at court; cross-jurisdiction appeals meant frontier banishment.

sentences.zh: 明言：「戍邊，防誣訴也。

translations.literal: Ming said: "Frontier banishment guards against false appeals.
translations.idiomatic: Ming said, "Frontier banishment guards against false appeals.

sentences.zh: 今訴不誣，法止當杖。

translations.literal: Now the appeal is not false; by law they should only be beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Now the appeal is not false; by law they should only be beaten.

sentences.zh: 」民有為妖言者，吏貪功，誣以謀反。

translations.literal: " Some spread demonic talk; clerks greedy for merit charged them with rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Some spread demonic talk; greedy clerks charged rebellion.

sentences.zh: 明按無反狀，止坐妖言律。

translations.literal: Ming investigated and found no rebellion; they were punished only under the demonic-talk statute.
translations.idiomatic: Ming found no rebellion; only demonic-talk punishment applied.

sentences.zh: 皆報許。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 巡撫河南，黜屬吏六十人。

translations.literal: Grand-coordinating Henan, he dismissed sixty subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Grand-coordinating Henan, he dismissed sixty subordinate officials.

sentences.zh: 再按畿輔，入總諸道章奏。

translations.literal: Inspecting the capital region a second time, he took charge of memorials from all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting the capital region again, he took charge of all circuit memorials.

sentences.zh: 天順初，尚書陳汝言有罪，偕諸御史劾，下之獄。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshun, Minister Chen Ruyan was guilty; together with the censors he impeached him and Ruyan was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshun's start Minister Chen Ruyan was impeached and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 四年，御史趙明等劾天下朝覲官，觸帝怒，詰草疏主名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year investigating censor Zhao Ming and others impeached officials attending court audience; this angered the Emperor, who demanded the drafter's name.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zhao Ming impeached audience officials; the Emperor demanded the drafter's name.

sentences.zh: 眾大懼，明獨自承。

translations.literal: All were greatly afraid; Ming alone took responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: All were afraid; Ming alone took responsibility.

sentences.zh: 都御史寇深言：「頻年章疏，盡出明手，幸勿以細故加罪。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Kou Shen said: "For years memorials have all come from Ming's hand; I beg you not punish him for a small matter."
translations.idiomatic: Kou Shen said, "Memorials have come from Ming; do not punish a small matter."

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，反稱明能。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind eased and he instead praised Ming's ability.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor eased and praised Ming's ability.

sentences.zh: 石亨既誅，僮仆皆收。

translations.literal: After Shi Heng was executed, all his servants were seized.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Heng was executed, all his servants were seized.

sentences.zh: 明言不宜，坐免者百人。

translations.literal: Ming said this was improper and a hundred men were spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Ming said this was improper and a hundred men were spared.

sentences.zh: 擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was raised to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Court of Judicial Review vice director.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，拜南京右僉都御史。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, Ming was appointed Nanjing right vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne, Ming was made Nanjing right vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 以留都春夏淫雨，請修人事以回天意。

translations.literal: Because the southern capital had excessive rain in spring and summer, he asked to repair human conduct to turn back Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: With excessive rain at the southern capital, he asked to repair human conduct to turn back Heaven's mind.

sentences.zh: 時納馬入監者至萬余人，明請區別。

translations.literal: At the time more than ten thousand who bought horses to enter the Directorate were enrolled; Ming asked that they be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand horse-buyers entered the Directorate; Ming asked distinction.

sentences.zh: 薦郎中孫瓊、陳鴻漸、梅倫、何宜，主事宋瑛，皆端方廉潔，恬於進取，宜顯擢以風有位。

translations.literal: He recommended Directors Sun Qiong, Chen Hongjian, Mei Lun, and He Yi and Chief Clerk Song Ying—all upright, honest, and content without advancement—worthy of promotion to admonish those in office.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Sun Qiong, Chen Hongjian, Mei Lun, He Yi, and Song Ying as upright men worthy of promotion.

sentences.zh: 疏下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 成化三年，揚州鹽寇起，守兵失利，詔明討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chenghua Yangzhou salt bandits rose; garrison troops were defeated; an edict ordered Ming to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 3 Yangzhou salt bandits rose; Ming was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 造巨艦，名曰「籌亭」，往來江上督戰，並江置邏堡候望。

translations.literal: He built great ships called "Planning Pavilions," patrolled the river supervising battle, and set watch forts along the river.
translations.idiomatic: He built "Planning Pavilion" ships, patrolled the river, and set watch forts.

sentences.zh: 賊縱跡無所匿，遂平之。

translations.literal: The bandits had nowhere to hide their tracks and were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits had nowhere to hide and were pacified.

sentences.zh: 內官鬻私鹽，據法沒入，鹽政大治。

translations.literal: Eunuchs sold private salt; he confiscated by law and salt administration was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs sold private salt; he confiscated by law and salt was ordered.

sentences.zh: 因條上利病十余事，多議行。

translations.literal: He then submitted more than ten items of benefit and harm; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten reform items; many were adopted.

sentences.zh: 仍還原任，以親老乞終養歸。

translations.literal: He still returned to his former post and, his parents being old, begged to nurture them and went home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to his post, then begged to nurture aged parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，上杭盜發。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year bandits rose in Shanghang.

sentences.zh: 詔起巡撫福建，督兵往討。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him to grand-coordinate Fujian and direct troops to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to grand-coordinate Fujian and campaign.

sentences.zh: 擒誅首惡，余皆減死遣戍。

translations.literal: He captured and executed ringleaders; the rest had sentences reduced and were sent to garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: He executed ringleaders; the rest were reduced and banished.

sentences.zh: 以上杭地接江西、廣東，盜易嘯聚，請析置永定縣。

translations.literal: Because Shanghang bordered Jiangxi and Guangdong and bandits easily gathered, he asked to establish Yongding county.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shanghang bordered Jiangxi and Guangdong he asked to establish Yongding county.

sentences.zh: 移疾徑歸。

translations.literal: Citing illness he went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness he went straight home.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he died.

sentences.zh: 楊繼宗，字承芳，陽城人。

translations.literal: Yang Jizong, styled Chengfang, was a man of Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jizong, whose style was Chengfang, came from Yangcheng.

sentences.zh: 天順初進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi at the start of Tianshun.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi at the start of Tianshun.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 囚多疫死，為時其食飲，令三日一櫛沐，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Many prisoners died of plague; he regularly supplied their food and drink and ordered bathing every three days; very many were saved.
translations.idiomatic: Many prisoners died of plague; he supplied food and ordered bathing every three days; many were saved.

sentences.zh: 又善辨疑獄。

translations.literal: He was also skilled at resolving doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled at resolving doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 河間獲盜，遣裏民張文、郭禮送京師，盜逸。

translations.literal: Hejian captured bandits and sent villagers Zhang Wen and Guo Li to the capital; the bandits escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian captured bandits and sent Zhang Wen and Guo Li to the capital; the bandits escaped.

sentences.zh: 文謂禮曰：「吾二人並當死。

translations.literal: Wen said to Li: "We two must both die.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said to Li, "We two must both die.

sentences.zh: 汝母老，鮮兄弟，以我代盜，庶全汝母子命。

translations.literal: Your mother is old and you have few brothers; let me replace the bandit so your mother and you may live.
translations.idiomatic: Your mother is old; let me replace the bandit so you may live.

sentences.zh: 」禮泣謝，從之。

translations.literal: " Li wept and thanked him and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li wept, thanked him, and agreed.

sentences.zh: 文桎梏詣部，繼宗察非盜，竟辨出之。

translations.literal: Wen came shackled to the ministry; Jizong saw he was not the bandit and finally argued him free.
translations.idiomatic: Wen came shackled; Jizong saw he was not the bandit and freed him.

sentences.zh: 成化初，用王翺薦，擢嘉興知府。

translations.literal: At the start of Chenghua, on Wang Ao's recommendation, he was raised to prefect of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenghua's start, on Wang Ao's recommendation, he was made Jiaxing prefect.

sentences.zh: 以一仆自隨，署齋蕭然。

translations.literal: He took only one servant; his office quarters were bare.
