translations.idiomatic: He took only one servant; his quarters were bare.

sentences.zh: 性剛廉孤峭，人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern, honest, and aloof; no one dared offend him.
translations.idiomatic: Stern, honest, and aloof, no one dared offend him.

sentences.zh: 而時時集父老問疾苦，為祛除之。

translations.literal: Yet he often gathered elders to ask their hardships and removed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gathered elders to ask hardships and removed them.

sentences.zh: 大興社學，民間子弟八歲不就學者，罰其父兄；

translations.literal: He greatly expanded community schools; if boys of eight did not study, their fathers and elder brothers were fined;
translations.idiomatic: He expanded community schools; boys of eight who did not study brought fines on kin;

sentences.zh: 遇學官以賓禮。

translations.literal: school officers were received with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: school officers were received as guests.

sentences.zh: 師儒競勸，文教大興。

translations.literal: Teachers competed in encouragement and literary culture flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Teachers competed in encouragement and culture flourished.

sentences.zh: 御史孔儒清軍，裏老多撻死。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Kong Ru cleared troops; many village elders were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Kong Ru cleared troops; many elders were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 繼宗榜曰：「御史杖人至死者，詣府報名。

translations.literal: Jizong posted a notice: "Censors who beat people to death must report to the prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Jizong posted: "Censors who beat people to death must report to the prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」儒怒。

translations.literal: " Ru was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Ru was angry.

sentences.zh: 繼宗入見曰：「為治有體。

translations.literal: Jizong came in and said: "Government has its proper form.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong said, "Government has its proper form.

sentences.zh: 公但剔奸弊，勸懲官吏。

translations.literal: You should only root out abuses and encourage and punish officials.
translations.idiomatic: You should root out abuses and punish officials.

sentences.zh: 若比戶稽核，則有司事，非憲體也。

translations.literal: House-by-house auditing is the local office's affair, not the censor's role."
translations.idiomatic: House-by-house auditing is local business, not a censor's role."

sentences.zh: 」儒不能難，而心甚銜之。

translations.literal: " Ru could not refute him but deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru could not refute him but resented him.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，突入府署，發篋視之，敝衣數襲而已。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he burst into the prefectural office, opened chests, and found only several suits of worn clothing.
translations.idiomatic: On departure he burst in, opened chests, and found only worn clothing.

sentences.zh: 儒慚而去。

translations.literal: Ru left ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Ru left ashamed.

sentences.zh: 中官過者，繼宗遺以菱芡、歷書。

translations.literal: When eunuchs passed through, Jizong gave them water chestnuts and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs passed, Jizong gave water chestnuts and calendars.

sentences.zh: 中官索錢，繼宗即發牒取庫金，曰：「金具在，與我印券。

translations.literal: When eunuchs asked for money, Jizong issued a warrant for treasury gold saying: "The gold is here; give me your stamped receipt."
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs asked for money, he issued for treasury gold saying, "Give me your receipt."

sentences.zh: 」中官咋舌不敢受。

translations.literal: The eunuchs gasped and dared not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs gasped and dared not take it.

sentences.zh: 入覲，汪直欲見之，不可。

translations.literal: On audience Wang Zhi wished to see him; he would not.
translations.idiomatic: On audience Wang Zhi wished to see him; he refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗問直：「朝覲官孰廉？

translations.literal: Xianzong asked Zhi: "Which audience official is honest?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong asked Zhi, "Which audience official is honest?"

sentences.zh: 」直對曰：「天下不愛錢者，惟楊繼宗一人耳。

translations.literal: " Zhi answered: "The only man in the realm who does not love money is Yang Jizong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi answered, "The only man who does not love money is Yang Jizong."

sentences.zh: 」九載秩滿，超遷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: " After nine years in office he was promoted over the regular steps to Zhejiang surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he was promoted to Zhejiang surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數與中官張慶忤。

translations.literal: He often clashed with the eunuch Zhang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He often clashed with eunuch Zhang Qing.

sentences.zh: 慶兄敏在司禮，每於帝前毀繼宗。

translations.literal: Qing's elder brother Min was in the Directorate of Ceremonial and often slandered Jizong before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qing's brother Min in the Directorate often slandered Jizong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「得非不私一錢之楊繼宗乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Is it not Yang Jizong, who keeps not a single cash?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Is it not Yang Jizong, who keeps not a coin?"

sentences.zh: 」敏惶恐，遺書慶曰：「善遇之，上已知其人矣。

translations.literal: " Min was frightened and wrote Qing: "Treat him well; the Emperor already knows the man."
translations.idiomatic: Min wrote Qing, "Treat him well; the Emperor knows him."

sentences.zh: 」聞母喪，立出。

translations.literal: " On news of his mother's death he left at once.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he left at once.

sentences.zh: 止驛亭下，盡籍廨中器物付有司。

translations.literal: He stopped only at the relay station and registered all office goods for the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped at the relay station and registered all office goods.

sentences.zh: 惟攜一仆、書數卷而還。

translations.literal: He took only one servant and several volumes of books in returning.
translations.idiomatic: He took one servant and several books home.

sentences.zh: 服除，以右僉都御史巡撫順天。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made right vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 畿內多權貴莊田，有侵民業者，輒奪還之。

translations.literal: Within the capital there were many estate fields of powerful families; where they encroached on people's property he seized and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: He returned estates powerful families had seized from the people.

sentences.zh: 按行關塞，武備大飭。

translations.literal: Inspecting passes and defenses, military readiness was greatly improved.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting defenses, he greatly improved military readiness.

sentences.zh: 星變，應詔陳言，歷指中官及文武諸臣貪殘狀，且請召還中官出鎮者。

translations.literal: When stars changed he memorialized on command, pointing out eunuchs' and civil and military officials' greedy cruelty and asking recall of eunuchs sent to garrison commands.
translations.idiomatic: On a celestial omen he listed eunuchs' and officials' greed and asked recall of garrison eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 益為權貴所嫉。

translations.literal: He was all the more envied by the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: He was all the more envied by the powerful.

sentences.zh: 治中陳翼訐其過，權貴因中之，左遷雲南副使。

translations.literal: Administration Vice Commissioner Chen Yi accused him of faults; the powerful struck through him and he was demoted Yunnan vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi accused him; the powerful struck and he was demoted to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 孝宗立，遷湖廣按察使。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne he was transferred Huguang surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong took the throne he was made Huguang surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既至，命汲水百斛，洗滌廳事而後視事，曰：「吾以除穢也。

translations.literal: On arrival he ordered a hundred hu of water drawn to wash the hall before conducting business, saying: "I am removing filth."
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he had the hall washed with a hundred hu of water, saying, "I remove filth."

sentences.zh: 」居無何，復以僉都御史巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: " Before long he was again made vice censor-in-chief grand coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again Yunnan grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 三司多舊僚，相見歡然。

translations.literal: Many in the three offices were old colleagues; meeting them was joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Many in the three offices were old colleagues; meeting was joyful.

sentences.zh: 既而出位揖之曰：「明日有公事，諸君幸相諒。

translations.literal: Then stepping out he bowed and said: "Tomorrow there is public business; I hope you will understand."
translations.idiomatic: Then he bowed and said, "Tomorrow is public business; please understand."

sentences.zh: 」遂劾罷不職者八人。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he impeached and dismissed eight incompetent men.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed eight incompetent men.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 繼宗力持風節，而居心慈厚，自處必以禮。

translations.literal: Jizong upheld integrity forcefully yet was kindly at heart and always conducted himself by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong upheld integrity yet was kindly and conducted himself by ritual.

sentences.zh: 為知府，謁上官必衣繡服，朝覲謁吏部亦然。

translations.literal: As prefect, visiting superiors he always wore embroidered robes, and so at audience at the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect he wore embroidered robes to visit superiors and at the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 或言不可，笑曰：「此朝廷法服也，此而不服，將安用之？

translations.literal: Some said he should not; he laughed: "This is the court's statutory dress; if I do not wear it, what is it for?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected; he laughed, "This is statutory dress—what else is it for?"

sentences.zh: 」為浙江按察時，倉官十余人坐缺糧系獄，至鬻子女以償。

translations.literal: As Zhejiang surveillance commissioner, more than ten granary officers were imprisoned for grain shortfalls and sold children to pay.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang commissioner, granary officers sold children to pay shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 繼宗欲寬之而無由。

translations.literal: Jizong wished to lenient them but had no means.
translations.idiomatic: Jizong wished to lenient them but had no means.

sentences.zh: 一日，送月俸至，命量之，則溢原數。

translations.literal: One day when monthly salary arrived he ordered it measured; it exceeded the original amount.
translations.idiomatic: One day his salary exceeded the original amount.

sentences.zh: 較他司亦然。

translations.literal: Comparing other offices it was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Other offices were the same.

sentences.zh: 因悟倉吏缺糧之由，將具實以聞。

translations.literal: He thus understood the cause of granary shortfalls and was about to report truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: He understood the cause of shortfalls and was about to report.

sentences.zh: 眾懼，請於繼宗，願捐俸代償。

translations.literal: All were afraid and begged Jizong to donate salary to pay.
translations.idiomatic: All begged Jizong to donate salary to pay.

sentences.zh: 由是十人者獲釋。

translations.literal: Thereby the ten men were released.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the ten were released.

sentences.zh: 嘗監鄉試得二卷，具朝服再拜曰：「二子當大魁天下，吾為朝廷得人賀耳。

translations.literal: Once supervising the provincial examination he obtained two papers, donned court robes, bowed twice and said: "These two will top the realm; I congratulate the court on gaining men."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising examinations he bowed to two papers saying they would top the realm.

sentences.zh: 」及拆卷，王華、李旻也，後果相繼為狀元。

translations.literal: When the papers were opened they were Wang Hua and Li Min; they indeed became top graduates in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They were Wang Hua and Li Min; they indeed became top graduates.

sentences.zh: 人服其鑒。

translations.literal: People admired his discernment.
translations.idiomatic: People admired his discernment.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，謚貞肅。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianqi he was given the posthumous title Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianqi's start he received the posthumous title Zhensu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：明初以十五布政司分治天下，諸邊要害則遣侯伯勛臣鎮扼之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In early Ming fifteen provincial administration commissions divided rule of the realm; on crucial frontiers marquis, earls, and meritorious ministers were sent to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Early Ming used fifteen provincial commissions; frontiers were garrisoned by meritorious nobles.

sentences.zh: 永樂之季，敕蹇義等二十六人巡行天下，安撫軍民，事竣還朝，不為經制。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongle an edict sent Jian Yi and twenty-six others to tour the realm pacifying soldiers and civilians; when finished they returned—not yet a regular institution.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongle's end Jian Yi and twenty-six others toured the realm—not yet regular.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，始命熊概巡撫蘇、松、兩浙。

translations.literal: At the start of Xuande Xiong Gai was first ordered to grand-coordinate Suzhou, Songjiang, and the two Zhe provinces.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuande's start Xiong Gai first grand-coordinated Suzhou, Songjiang, and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 越數年，而江西、河南諸省以次專設巡撫官。

translations.literal: Within several years Jiangxi, Henan, and other provinces successively had dedicated grand coordinator posts.
translations.idiomatic: Within years Jiangxi, Henan, and others gained dedicated grand coordinators.

sentences.zh: 天順初，暫罷復設，諸邊亦稍用廷臣出鎮或參贊軍務。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianshun they were briefly abolished and restored; frontiers also gradually used court ministers to garrison or join military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianshun's start they were briefly abolished and restored; frontiers used court ministers.

sentences.zh: 蓋以地大物眾，法令滋章，三司謹奉教條，修其常職；

translations.literal: Because the land was vast and population large and laws multiplied, the three offices carefully followed regulations and performed routine duties;
translations.idiomatic: Because the land was vast and laws multiplied, the three offices kept routine duties;

sentences.zh: 而興利除弊，均賦稅，擊貪濁，安善良，惟巡撫得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: but to promote benefit, remove harm, equalize taxes, strike corruption, and settle the good, only grand coordinators could act conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: but to promote benefit, equalize taxes, and strike corruption, only grand coordinators could act conveniently.

sentences.zh: 熊概以下諸人，強幹者立聲威，愷悌者流惠愛，政績均有可紀。

translations.literal: From Xiong Gai onward, the forceful established authority, the kind spread benevolence, and all had achievements worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiong Gai onward, the forceful established authority and the kind spread benevolence—all worth recording.

sentences.zh: 于謙、周忱巡撫最為有名，而勛業尤盛，故別著焉。

translations.literal: Yu Qian and Zhou Chen as grand coordinators were most famous, but their achievements were especially great and are treated separately.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qian and Zhou Chen were the most renowned grand coordinators, yet their achievements were so great they are given separate treatment.
